articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts: Michael van Gerwen books James Wade last-16 clash as Luke Humphries, Nathan Aspinall also progress
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen edges final group stage clash with Jeffrey de Graaf; Luke Humphries, Nathan Aspinall and Gian van Veen also secure safe passage through to last 16; watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports, with the final on Sunday November 22
articles.body:
During Van Gerwen's 5-4 victory over Jeffrey de Graaf it became apparant that the Dutchman had done enough to qualify even if he didn't ultimately win, but his late wobble will still be a concern as he missed seven match darts.

In twice breaking De Graaf's throw - at one stage leading 3-1, and to go 4-3 up - Van Gerwen ensured he would top Group L even if he went on lose 5-4, as he held the tiebreaker in winning the most legs against the throw.

Ultimately, that tiebreaker wasn't neccesary, despite MVG's spurning of several match darts across a couple of legs before he finally landed his eighth.

The three-time Grand Slam champion has booked a meeting with three-time runner-up Wade in the next round, a rematch of the pair's meeting in the 2016 final, which the Dutchman won.

"It wasn't a good game at all," Van Gerwen told Sky Sports after his win. "I messed up! What can I say, I am through to the next round and onto the next one.

"James Wade is playing some fantastic darts. I need to bring my A-game if I am going to beat him, simple as that."

Wade enjoyed a much easier time of things in his winner-takes all shootout with 'Rapid' Ricky Evans in Group K, dispatching of his opponent with such speed as to make a mockery of his nickname.

'The Machine' has dropped only one leg over his two group stage wins, averaging over 100 in both, having beaten Cam Crabtree 5-1 in his opener.

What else happened on Tuesday at the Grand Slam?

Nathan Aspinall replicated Wade's route through to the last 16 as he too rounded off a couple of superb performances in the group stage with a 5-0 whitewash of Karel Sedlacek.

He also only dropped one leg in his opening match against Maik Kuivenhoven, in which he averaged 111.68, following that up with another ton-plus average against Sedlacek.

"I am sick of being the nearly man," Aspinall told Sky Sports . "People talk about how good I am but I don't win anything. I want that to change that next year. Hopefully this is the start of a good week."

The 11th seed will face Gabriel Clemens in the next round after his 5-3 victory over Rusty-Jake Rodriguez, who had a dart at double to claim a fourth leg in the match, which would have secured his progress at Clemens' expense.

German No 1 Martin Schindler joins his countryman in the last 16 after knocking out Chris Dobey with a 5-3 win in their Group N shootout.

He now meets No 3 seed Gian van Veen in the knockout stage after he got the better of Bradley Brooks 5-2 to round off Group M.

And the last 16 line-up is completed with a meeting of 2023 champion Luke Humphries and Tom Sykes after the former world No 1 beat Joe Cullen 5-2 to ensure his passage through. Sykes, meanwhile, started the night with a 5-1 victory over Krzysztof Ratajski in their winner-takes-all clash.

articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts results: Luke Humphries and Michael van Gerwen reach last 16
articles.summary: Luke Humphries and Michael van Gerwen book their places in the last 16 of the Grand Slam of Darts with victories in their final group matches.
articles.body:
Luke Humphries and Michael van Gerwen booked their places in the last 16 of the Grand Slam of Darts with victories in their final group matches.

Humphries beat fellow Englishman Joe Cullen 5-2 despite averaging 98.67 to his opponent's 103.22.

The former world champion will now face compatriot Tom Sykes, the lowest-ranked player remaining in the tournament, after he defeated Krzysztof Ratajski 5-1 to top Group J.

Van Gerwen was well below his best as he scraped past Sweden's Jeffrey de Graaf 5-4.

The Dutchman missed several match darts at 4-3 up, allowing De Graaf to force a deciding leg.

However, Van Gerwen regrouped to seal victory and set up a last-16 meeting with James Wade.

"It wasn't a good game at all. We were both under pressure and that didn't do us any favours," Van Gerwen said.

"Sometimes you don't do what you want to do. That's frustrating because I know I am capable of a lot more."

Elsewhere, Wade, Gian van Veen and Nathan Aspinall all made light work of their opponents to secure their places in the knockout stage.

articles.title: WWE NXT Results, Winners, Live Grades, Reaction, Highlights From November 17
articles.summary: As the John Cena Classic continues to take shape, the next several weeks of WWE NXT could see more names announced for the upcoming competition.
articles.body:
As the John Cena Classic continues to take shape, the next several weeks of WWE NXT could see more names announced for the upcoming competition.

Among those already confirmed to take part is Kelani Jordan, who will defend her NXT Women's Championship for the third time in under three weeks against former champ Kendal Grey. Their initial encounter at Heatwave at the end of August was a barn burner and this highly-anticipated rematch should be no different.

Another ex-champ in Tony D'Angelo will also be in action as he takes on the frustrated Kam Hendrix, who is on a mission to prove himself against NXT's biggest fan favorites despite consistently coming up short.

Elsewhere on the card, Zilla Fatu will face off with DarkState's Dion Lennox while Saquon Shugars, Tristan Angels and Sean Legacy collide in a Triple Threat match.

Here are the complete results, grades and reaction for the Nov. 17 edition of WWE NXT as it airs live on The CW.

Last Time in Action: Grayson Waller def. Tony D'Angelo (Halloween Havoc, Oct. 31); EK Prosper def. Kam Hendrix (NXT, Nov. 10) .

Unsure of his next move after failing to regain the NXT Championship from Grayson Waller at Halloween Havoc, Tony D'Angelo was attacked by Kam Hendrix (who had just been beaten by EK Prosper) backstage last week on NXT.

These two previously met for the NXT Championship on NXT TV earlier in the year, a match that was won by D'Angelo.

D'Angelo attacked Lennox before the bell and wasted no time in laying the boots to him. D'Angelo dominated the early goings, and whenever Hendrix briefly got the upper-hand, he showboated instead of taking advantage.

It got more competitive once Hendrix went into serious mode, though D'Angelo later leveled him with a top rope superplex. D'Angelo went on to nail a Spear for a close two count, and upon kicking out, Hendrix went to ringside and started wrecking havoc with a steel chair.

Myles Borne prevented D'Angelo from using it himself, allowing Hendrix to plant D'Angelo on the chair before hitting his Lights, Kam, Action finisher in the ring for the win.

NXT officials are clearly high on Hendrix, but if they want fans to take him seriously, he needs to rack up some meaningful wins. Thus, this was a step in the right direction for him.

D'Angelo has been on the NXT brand for over five years now. Surely he's headed to the main roster soon, right? It would explain why he's putting over so many people on the way out.

Borne adopting a darker attitude has been the best thing for his career, and pairing him in a program with D'Angelo should put him in an even better spot on the show once it's over. This was a nice match to give Hendrix a win while also furthering the story between Borne and D'Angelo.

Zaria said that Izzi Dame has successfully done what she set out to do: making her life a living hell. In doing so, she's simultaneously exposed herself as a bully, something Zaria has been no stranger to throughout her journey.

She aggressively called out Dame, who emerged wearing the John Cena Classic jacket she was just gifted by John Cena earlier in the day. She reminded Zaria not only will she be a part of the upcoming Classic but also that she's emotionally unstable and that the NXT Women's North American Championship belongs around her waist.

Zaria told her she's not a good person and that she's done with the psychological warfare. She granted her a shot at the title and said it will be an opportunity to prove herself as being unbothered, unstoppable and unshakable before planting her with an F5.

The dynamic of this feud remains a mess. Both of them being heels isn't the issue as much as the story that fans are supposed to root for Zaria against the big bully, despite Zaria betraying her best friend Sol Ruca earlier this year and not being the best person herself.

That said, this was a solid segment from these two to set up their rematch, where the Women's North American title will actually be on the line this time. Zaria should definitely retain as Dame still isn't that interesting of a character, even though she's made strides in the ring over the last year or so.

Dame is a good get for the John Cena Classic, but there's virtually no chance she wins if it's indeed going to be a glorified popularity contest. If spots for the NXT talent are limited, then there were better options than Dame.

Last Time in Action: Lizzy Rain def. Chantel Monroe (NXT, Nov. 10); Izzi Dame def. Layla Diggs (NXT, Oct. 20) .

Following a bit of a back-and-forth from Chantel Monroe and Layla Diggs early on, Monroe hit a great-looking draping DDT on Diggs off the second rope. Diggs retaliated with a DDT of her own shortly thereafter.

Diggs landed more impressive offense, including a moonsault off the apron. Just as the crowd began to rally behind her, Monroe hit her with a modified neckbreaker for the three count.

This was short and sweet, pretty much as it should have been. Both women are works in progress, so there was no reason to have this last longer than it did to potentially expose their weaknesses. They had impressive outings here.

Monroe has been featured fairly frequently on NXT TV over the last month, and this is the second win she's scored after already beating Izzi Dame. Consistency will the key to her success, and so far, she's been handled well.

Diggs should get more character development at some point. She's essentially a stepping stone in the women's division at the moment and that's a fine role for her for now, but she deserves a chance to show what she can do on the mic as there's been some glimmers of greatness with her in-ring work.

Ranking WWE and AEW's Most Underrated Stars of 2026 🌟

Last Time in Action: Zilla Fatu def. Charlie Dempsey (Halloween Havoc, Oct. 31); Cruz Montana def. Dion Lennox (NXT, Nov. 4) .

There isn't much bad blood between these two as of now, yet Zilla Fatu went right after Lennox out of the gate. Lennox maintained the advantage coming out of the commercial break but was eventually put down by a thunderous Samoan Drop from Fatu.

A running senton from Fatu wasn't enough to earn him the win, either. He channeled his father Umaga with a running hip attack in the corner but missed the diving splash from the top rope.

Lennox hit a vicious lariat as well as a fisherman's suplex for a strong nearfall. Once Karmen Petrovic popped up on the platform in the distance, the rest of Perros del Mal rushed the ring and took out DarkSate.

With Lennox distracted, Fatu connected with his Triple Z running forearm smash as well as his signature splash to emerge victorious.

Although this match was more of a backdrop to further the feud between DarkState and Perros del Mal, it ended up being an enjoyable encounter. Fatu is a star on the rise and Lennox is improving at a rather rapid rate as well. They worked well together and hopefully they'll face off again down the road.

The latest faction warfare has potential based on how crowds have reacted to their last two brawls. It's a shame WarGames is now property of the main roster because it would actually made sense in this situation.

Fatu is basically killing time until the John Cena Classic, where he's easily the top favorite from NXT to win the whole thing. He's certainly popular enough, and the NXT Championship is unquestionably in his future if he can keep trending in that direction.

Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno Address The Vanity Project

Noam Dar and Romeo Moreno were out in the ring to start the segment with their Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic trophy. Dar said they've been on a hyperspeed run after taking the trophy and being announced for the John Cena Classic and that they should be celebrating but aren't because The Vanity Project prevented them from challenging for the NXT Tag Team Championship last week.

Moreno said it's destiny to become champions and that they wanted their shot tonight. They get Hank Walker and Tank Ledger instead, who told them that they would've won the tag titles last week had Dar and Moreno not interfered in their match versus Vanity Project.

Vanity Project interrupted their bickering with Ricky Smokes saying that they usually have women fighting over them. In fact, Dar and Moreno repaid them for the aforementioned attack by unintentionally helping them retain the tag titles against Hank and Tank.

Their stirring of the pot ended up uniting Dar, Moreno, Walker and Ledger, with Robert Stone then announcing an eight-man tag team match for next week. He instructed Vanity Project to find a fourth man, but Myka Lockwood spoke up and said there was no need because she'd make her in-ring debut and serve as their partner.

We don't often get talking segments with the tag teams of NXT, so this was a refreshing change of pace. It was a logical development for the tag title picture with both the duo of Dar and Moreno as well as Hank and Tank hot on the heels of Vanity Project.

Both Dar and Moreno both being in the John Cena Classic should be interesting. They'll likely be in there to have fun matches more than anything, as it's safe to assume fans aren't going to vote for them over others. At least it's a smart way to capitalize on their momentum.

Lockwood finally wrestling next week feels like a genuine attraction. She won't feel out of place in there with the guys whatsoever. Is it too late to get her in the John Cena Classic, too?

Saquon Shugars vs. Tristan Angels vs. Sean Legacy

Last Time in Action: Sean Legacy def. Saquon Shugars (NXT, Oct. 27); Tristan Angels def. Shugars (NXT, Oct. 13) .

Saquon Shugars won his feud with Dion Lennox not long ago, but in struggling to find his confidence, he's lost singles matches to the likes of Tristan Angels and Sean Legacy. This was his chance to redeem himself by avenging those losses.

This was a fun Triple Threat where they kept the pace consistent throughout. In the first half, Shugars and Legact ensured Angels was kept at bay while battling each other, which led to Angels dumping them to ringside right before the break.

All three traded offense in an attempt to gain the upper-hand. A smooth dropkick combo from Shugars laid out Legacy, but after Shugars hit him with another kick through the ropes, Angels capitalized by rolling up Legacy and stealing the win before Shugars could break up the pin.

Tristan Angels defeated Sean Legacy and Saquon Shugars.

Shugars loses again. He'll be fine provided this is actually leading somewhere, but it's certainly a choice to have him lose so many matches after building momentum as a singles star following his feud with DarkState.

Speaking of shortcomings, Angels has done a lot of losing in 2026, so this was a much-needed win for him. He's a quality midcard heel but just needs more credibility. He'll get his comeuppance from Shugars eventually, but it will mean more if he stays winning until then.

More tension was teased between Shugars and Legacy afterward, so we'll likely get another one-on-one matchup between them soon. A heel turn from Legacy is possible, but he feels more natural as a face.

NXT Women's Championship: Kelani Jordan vs. Kendal Grey

Last Time in Action: Kelani Jordan def. Paige (NXT, Nov. 4); Jordan def. Kendal Grey (Heatwave, Aug. 31).

This is Kendal Grey's first bout back since being cleared by medical. She targeted Kelani Jordan's ankle in the opening minutes, but Jordan quickly reached the ropes to break it up.

When Jordan failed to suplex her into the ring from the apron, she pivoted and hit a springboard frog splash onto Grey's ankle. Post-commercial, Grey unleashed a flurry of offense and hit an awesome facebuster out of the corner for a two count.

Jordan walked over to the NXT Women's Championship belt at ringside but was thrown back into the ring by Grey. Grey secured another ankle lock but Jordan got out of it, only to to toss Grey into the turnbuckle post and hit a frog splash and an immediate 450 splash.

Grey continued to go for her patented ankle lock but was thwarted at every turn. She even connected with a Shades of Grey off the top rope, but Jordan kicked out to a big pop from the crowd.

Grey's final ankle lock was her most effective, but before Jordan could tap, Jordan slapped the referee and intentionally got herself disqualified to retain the title.

Kendal Grey defeated Kelani Jordan by disqualification; Jordan retained the NXT Women's Championship.

The "This is awesome" chants from the crowd were well deserved. Grey and Jordan had a heck of a war at Heatwave and this was equally excellent. Props to them for such a stellar main event.

Grey came so close to clinching the title here that every nearfalls and submission hold of hers was believable. Disqualification finishes are rarely satisfying, but this one was well executed as it made Jordan look cunning and Grey sympathetic. Their chemistry is simply off the charts.

Doing a title change in the main event of NXT TV would have been huge, but it's safe to assume this is building toward one final clash at TLC, likely with some sort of a stipulation. With Jordan taking part in the John Cena Classic that Monday on Raw, TLC should be where Grey regains the gold.

This was a solid edition of NXT TV made significantly better by its hot main event. Grey and Jordan are the standouts of not only the women's division but the entire show at the moment, with NXT champion Grayson Waller taking a bit of a backseat until his next challenger is determined.

Along with Izzi Dame, Shiloh Hill was also confirmed for the John Cena Classic. The announcements have been newsworthy (even if they're pre-taped), though it's unknown what's going into these decisions for selections and who will benefit from being a part of it once it's over.

The rest of this episode was adequate and set the stage for what could be an above-average show next week with Hill vs. Mason Rook in the NXT Championship number one contender's match, the eight-person tag team matchup, and Zaria vs. Dame for the NXT Women's North American Championship all being advertised.

Being in a rebuilding phase, NXT needs to elevate a few more fresh faces and give some of these storylines more juice. In the meantime, they're filling the two hours better than they have in the past.

Graham Mirmina, aka Graham "GSM" Matthews, has specialized in sports and entertainment writing since 2010. Visit his website, WrestleRant , and subscribe to his YouTube channel for more wrestling-related content.

articles.title: Controversy! Magnus Carlsen forfeits Fast Classic game against Kazakhstan's Bibisara Assaubayeva, calls it 'totally useless'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Magnus Carlsen was involved in another controversy at the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest after forfeiting his Fast
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Magnus Carlsen was involved in another controversy at the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest after forfeiting his Fast Classic game against Kazakhstan's Bibisara Assaubayeva on Tuesday.The Norwegian grandmaster decided not to play the game after securing the day's result through blitz and rapid games. The unplayed Fast Classic game had no impact on his classical rating, as forfeited games are not included in rating calculations.Carlsen won the first three blitz games and drew the fourth before winning both rapid games. This gave him an 11.5-0.5 lead. With only eight points available in the Fast Classic game, Assaubayeva could no longer win the day's contest.Assaubayeva was awarded the victory by forfeit, leaving Carlsen with an 11.5-8.5 win for the day.Carlsen, who was scheduled to play with White, explained his decision to Norwegian broadcaster TV2. He said there was no point playing a game that could no longer change the result.“There will be no classical game as I understood, the match is over. The only consequence of not showing up is that you will lose a totally useless game. I think that if you play a World Championship and it counts for points and such, I can understand,” Carlsen said.“In the end, if you play games after, it shall not be rated because it’s always been like that. And if they want to do things differently here. This is my decision on this topic.”Why did Carlsen forfeit the game?Carlsen's decision came after a difficult run in the Fast Classic format at the Budapest event. The 35-year-old had struggled during the five-day group stage, where he failed to win any of his 10 games. He drew nine games and lost one against Armenia's Haik Martirosyan.The results cost him 21.8 Elo points, taking his live classical rating to 2801.2. He finished fifth in Group C and came close to dropping below the 2800 rating mark.American grandmaster Fabiano Caruana also came close to overtaking Carlsen as the World No. 1 in the classical ratings during the group stage.The decision to forfeit the game against Assaubayeva also meant Carlsen avoided another possible rating loss. A draw would have cost him 3.5 rating points, while an over-the-board defeat would have cost him 8.5 points.However, Carlsen said his decision was based on his objection to playing a game that would not count towards the classical rating after the day's result had already been decided.Under FIDE's rating regulations, unplayed games, including forfeits, are not included in rating calculations. As a result, Assaubayeva received the tournament points for the game, but neither player's classical rating was affected.What is Fast Classic chess?Fast Classic is an accelerated form of classical chess. Players start with 45 minutes on their clock and receive a 30-second increment after every move.The format was part of the Total Chess World Championship Tour Pilot in Budapest. Unlike regular classical chess, the shorter time control makes the games faster while still requiring players to manage their time and make decisions under pressure.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Knicks pull off Toronto sweep thanks to Jalen Brunson’s late 4-point play
articles.summary: Jalen Brunson snatched another victory in Canada with a pivotal sequence.
articles.body:
TORONTO — The Knicks channeled their inner Drake by going "Back to Back" in Toronto.

With Canada's famous rapper sitting courtside inside Scotiabank Arena, Jalen Brunson again snatched victory from the Raptors with a momentous late sequence.

The point guard pulled up for a 3-pointer with 1:25 remaining in a close game, which he buried while being flagrantly fouled because defender Ja'Kobe Walter stepped into Brunson's landing space.

The result was a 4-point play for Brunson and possession retained by the Knicks, who were fouled and quickly made two more free throws, courtesy of Landry Shamet, to basically put away their 111-102 victory .

That six-point swing meant the Knicks left Canada with two wins in three days.

"That created the separation that we needed to be able to put them away," coach Mike Brown said. "So just a big shot. It was one of those things where the play broke down, and we kept looking for an opportunity while spacing the floor. And Jalen found one and let it fly."

Brunson crumbled to the floor because of a twisted ankle, but bounced up, walked to the bench while the refs reviewed the foul, and recovered to hit the foul shot.

"Adrenaline was pumping," he said, "and went back out there."

It followed Brunson's big trey to beat the Raptors on Sunday, reinforcing the Knicks' dominance over their division foe.

The Knicks (8-6) have won 15 straight against the Raptors (5-9), a streak dating to 2023. But Toronto entered Tuesday confident about its chances after stretching the Knicks into overtime Sunday.

"After rewatching and rewatching and rewatching film, we played against the NBA champions and, in my 3 ¹/₂ years here as coach, that's when we came the closest to beating them," Raptors coach Darko Rajaković said. "We're getting better. Just one free throw and the game is completely different."

He finished with 31 points in 34 minutes on 10-for-22 shooting. Karl-Anthony Towns recorded his 14th straight double-double to start the season — a franchise record — dropping 16 points with 16 rebounds.

The Knicks closed the game with a 9-0 run, which followed their 19-0 run to end the first half.

After struggling in the clutch to start the season, the Knicks rediscovered their clutch gene in Toronto.

"A lot of times when we get in games like that, especially last year, the cardiac Knicks find a way," Towns said.

Bridges put together a third consecutive strong performance with 17 points in 30 minutes. Josh Hart scored his first points in three games , dropping five in 31 minutes. Landry Shamet continued his hot November with 12 points and was a team-best plus-26.

After a four-day stop in Canada, Brown left satisfied with a team win — solidified by an important Brunson moment.

"I thought our execution, especially down the stretch, the last few minutes of the game, was at a pretty high level," the coach said, "on both ends of the floor, but particularly offensively. Our pacing, our spacing, our screening — we took care of the basketball down the stretch.

"We got a lot of different guys that produced in a lot of different ways tonight. Obviously, KAT continues to be a double-double machine. OG [Anunoby] was our defensive player of the game. … Mikal was good for us, especially down the stretch. And Landry Shamet was huge."

articles.title: Warriors Superstar Stephen Curry Shares Details of Last Season’s Knee Injury
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors are struggling amid the absence of superstar guard Stephen Curry, who is recovering from a right oblique abdominal tear.Curry misse...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors are struggling amid the absence of superstar guard Stephen Curry, who is recovering from a right oblique abdominal tear.

Curry missed his second straight game on Monday as the Warriors suffered another blowout loss, this time against the New Orleans Pelicans.

The Warriors will be without Curry until Thanksgiving, though it's possible he could be sidelined for an even longer period, as per BasketNews.

Stephen Curry Opens Up About Knee Injury

GettySteph Curry #30 of the Golden State Warriors reacts after making a basket against the Los Angeles Lakers at Chase Center on October 30, 2026 in San Francisco, California.

Last season, Stephen Curry missed 39 games last season due to rest, minor issues and a major knee injury. Curry was out for 27 consecutive games after being diagnosed with patellofemoral pain syndrome in his right knee, more commonly known as runner's knee.

Speaking to ESPN's Anthony Slater , Curry shared how painful the injury was and the setbacks he suffered during his adjustment and recovery from what was described as a chronic issue the two-time MVP will have to play with for the rest of his career.

"Against Detroit, it took everything in me down there on the training table just to be like, 'Oh, I can go out here tonight and play,'" Curry said. "And I was just faking it for the first whatever (25 minutes)."

The Warriors superstar tried to return after the All-Star break and even worked out with Sabrina Ionescu . However, "there were certain directions of movement and stuff that just didn't work," so his return was pushed back.

Curry was supposed to scrimmage with the team in late March, but his right knee "felt worse than it had before." He called it a "true setback," though he managed to come back before the end of the regular season.

The Warriors labored to make the NBA play-in tournament. They shocked the LA Clippers to have a shot at the No. 8 spot, but they were blown out by the Phoenix Suns .

In the same interview with ESPN's Anthony Slater, Stephen Curry admitted that the two-year, $115 million extension he signed in the offseason could be his last.

"I assumed that it would probably be one of, if not the last, contract I signed," Curry said. "I'm not afraid to say it. But maybe I'll surprise myself and want to keep going."

At the age of 38, Curry was playing at an MVP level before his oblique injury.

And with the way the Warriors lost their first two games since the injury, they still need their superstar more than ever.

articles.title: Cincinnati schedules home-and-home with Missouri for 2027 and 2032
articles.summary: Cincinnati and Mizzou will meet for the first time ever next September.
articles.body:
While the 2026 regular season is in its twilight stages, some teams are already looking ahead to 2027.

On Tuesday, Cincinnati and Missouri announced a home-and-home non-conference series. Missouri will host the Bearcats at Faurot Field on Sept. 18, 2027, while Cincinnati welcomes the Tigers to Nippert Stadium on Sept. 11, 2032.

Although the campuses are separated by fewer than 500 miles, the 2027 matchup will mark the first-ever meeting between the Big 12 and SEC opponents.

Cincinnati has now finalized its non-conference schedule for the 2027 season. The Bearcats will host Central Connecticut of the FCS on Aug. 28, remain at home against Missouri State on Sept. 4, and complete their non-conference slate at Missouri on Sept. 18. Cincinnati does not have a game scheduled for the weekend of Sept. 11, when it will either play its Big 12 opener or take a bye.

Both Missouri and Cincinnati experienced recent cancelations in their 2027 non-conference slates, making them a perfect match for each other. The Tigers saw their 2027 home contest against Illinois get axed, while Cincinnati's looming road trip to Boston College was also removed from the schedule.

The Bearcats have won five consecutive regular season non-conference matchups, sweeping all three opponents during the 2026 season. The 2027 trip to Missouri will mark the program's first true road non-conference game since Sept. 14, 2024 when it traveled to crosstown rival Miami (OH). Also, it will be the Bearcats' first out-of-state non-conference road game since Sept. 9, 2023 at Pittsburgh and first SEC matchup since Sept. 3, 2022 at Arkansas.

Cincinnati traditionally had one non-conference vacancy reserved for Miami, as the two competed in one of the longest running series in college football. The rivals played their 129th and final scheduled meeting this past September, making it the fourth-most played FBS matchup behind Minnesota-Wisconsin, Auburn-Georgia, and North Carolina-Virginia.

Although an iconic rivalry has been shelved, the Bearcats can look forward to securing their first victory over SEC competition on Sept. 18, 2027 in Columbia.

articles.title: You’ve Been Serb’d: Illinois 99, Duke 78
articles.summary: Duke took a beating, and didn’t deserve to win this game. Congrats to Illinois.
articles.body:
First of all, there's no doubt that Illinos deserved the win at Cameron on Tuesday night. The Illini just thumped the Blue Devils in almost every way. They outrebounded Duke, 54-34, and Duke had 14 turnovers. Illinois also outscored Duke 31-21 from the line, and ruthlessly controlled the paint. Duke took 40 threes in this game, hitting just 9. Illinois shot just 6-32, but their control of the paint made that irrelevant. And so did the performance of Andrej Stojakovic.

When Duke played Cal in 2024, Stojakovic finished with 10 points on 4-14. Tuesday night, he lit Duke up for 46 points on 14-21/2-3 from the floor, along with 16-20 from the free throw line.

It was a record-breaking performance: the most points ever scored by an opponent in Cameron was 43 by South Carolina's Grady Wallace in 1957, when the ACC was 3 years, 9 months, and 15 days old.

It came perilously close to breaking Dick Groats' record of 48 points, set in 1952.

He was superb and nearly unguardable, but he's not the only reason that Illinois won. Quentin Coleman racked up 27, but it was more than that.

Here's something you may not have caught: Zavier Zens, cousin of Kon and Kager Knueppel, who is 6-7, got 8 rebounds. He out-rebounded every Duke player who got on the floor. So did Coleman, who is 6-4, and so did reserve Stevan Vaaks, who, like Zens, is 6-7.

JoJo Boumtje Boumtje got 5 rebounds. He's 7-2. Patrick Ngongba got 4 rebounds. He's 6-11. Cameron Williams, 7-0, got 3. Drew Scharnowski, 6-10, got 2.

Three players, all 6-7 or under, and two of them freshmen, outrebounded Duke's stable of big men. The leading rebounder for Duke?

Basically, the same thing happened with Illinois that happened at Michigan State: both teams were significantly tougher and more focused than was Duke, and the Blue Devils paid the price.

At the half, Scheyer pulled two starters: Boumtje Boumtje and Cayden Boozer, opting for Foster and Sebastian Wilkins instead.

Wilkins has played very well all season, and deserved his shot, and Foster is highly reliable, but it didn't make any difference, because Stojakovic stayed red hot, and to a lesser extent, so did Coleman.

Those two finished with 73 of the 99 Illinois hung up in Cameron.

It was a dismal night, but nonetheless, there were some bright moments. You could argue that Duke's second five outplayed the starters. Cameron Williams came in and almost immediately blocked two shots. That's at least the second time he's done that, and possibly the third. He has great instincts for blocks.

Scharnowski hit a three, which, we believe, was the first he's ever hit in college. He played hard and certainly didn't back down. Deron Rippey didn't score, but he had 7 assists to two turnovers. And when Bryson Howard was in, he may have defended Stojakovic more effectively than anyone else on the team. He really gave him trouble in a way no one else did.

We've already talked about Wilkins and Foster, but we should say this about Wilkins: he's looking better and better. He moves incredibly well on the court, he defends, and he's the furthest thing from selfish.

We're not sure what lessons Jon Scheyer will draw from this game, but from our vantage point, we saw that Duke was soft inside. And until that gets fixed, there are going to be games like this.

We've seen enough of Ngongba to know that a bad game doesn't mean the next one will be bad, too, but we can't say that about Boumtje Boumtje.

Clearly, he's got a perimeter game, but 7-2 is a gift from God that one shouldn't squander. In the second half, he was far more willing to take it to Illinois, and got to the line as a result. At whatever point he gets mad enough to rip someone's head off on a dunk, you'll know that part of the problem with this team has been solved.

Side note: remember when Dahntay Jones did pushups after that insane dunk against Virginia?

The reason he did it was because he was angry at his coach, Mike Krzyzewski, who had challenged him in some pretty elemental ways, as we understand it, and Jones wanted to make a point.

We're not sure how Scheyer will do that, but it might need to be done.

And in fairness to Boumtje Boumtje, and we're not picking on him, but the kid is 17. He's adapting to a very new situation. Let's give them both time and space to figure that out.

The reality though is that in sports, there's a goal, and that goal is to win. As we saw in the second half, sometimes changes need to be made. It's going to be hard not to give minutes to Williams, Scharnowski, Howard, and most of all, Wilkins, if the starters let themselves get pushed around.

Notes – Scheyer got a technical in the first half, which we think is his third as head coach…so did Dame Sarr…people are upset about the loss, but remember that Coach K took some beatings during his long and storied career…we wouldn't judge this team in November…not only was that Scharnowski's first made three, but it looks like it's the only one he's taken in three years…we'd love to see Blackwell go off soon…

articles.title: ‘Ridiculous’: Dale Earnhardt Jr. Shuts Down Chase Elliott Crew Chief Criticism
articles.summary: Dale Earnhardt Jr. defended the driver/crew chief pairing of Chase Elliott and Alan Gustafson in the wake of Hendrick Motorsports’ 2027 lineup change. While...
articles.body:
Dale Earnhardt Jr. defended the driver/crew chief pairing of Chase Elliott and Alan Gustafson in the wake of Hendrick Motorsports' 2027 lineup change. While HMS drivers William Byron and Alex Bowman are getting different crew chiefs, Elliott and Gustafson remain together for 2027.

On Monday, it was announced that Rudy Fugle will be atop the pit box for Bowman in 2027 after six seasons as Byron's crew chief. Adam Wall, who was the crew chief for Corey Day in the NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series, will move up to the Cup level as Byron's crew chief in 2027.

Meanwhile, the pairing of Elliott and Gustafson, as well as Kyle Larson and Cliff Daniels, will stay together next year.

Earnhardt Jr. Fires Back at Elliott, Gustafson Criticism: 'None of Y'all's Business'

Earnhardt Jr. discussed the shake-up at Hendrick Motorsports on the recent episode of "The Dale Jr. Download."

The former HMS driver said that some fans might look at the news of the crew chief changes and be angered by the fact Gustafson will continue to be Elliott's crew chief next year.

In the wake of the news, some fans have voiced their frustrations on social media under an X post by motorsports reporter Jeff Gluck regarding the matter .

The NASCAR Hall of Famer dismissed those voices, noting that the two enjoy working with each other. Earnhardt Jr. was blunt in saying the partnership is nobody else's business besides the people involved.

"There's this small little group of people that are seeing this news and going, 'They're going to leave Chase and Alan together still?' It's ridiculous. Chase and Alan want to work together. It's their [expletive] choice. None of y'all's business," Earnhardt Jr. said.

Earnhardt Jr. noted that Elliott has been on record saying he enjoys working with Gustafson and questioned why there is so much criticism around the crew chief.

"Chase likes it. He's said it multiple times. He likes Alan. What are we missing?"

Earnhardt Jr. acknowledges that fans are allowed to have an opinion and do not know the full behind-the-scenes story with things like this. However, because Elliott has expressed his desire to work with Gustafson

Therefore, Earnhardt Jr. believes fans should give the pairing a break.

"This is something that Chase, multiple times, has said, 'I want to work with him. He's great.' Let's just leave it alone," Earnhardt Jr. said.

Chase Elliott Hit Career Lows During 2026 Season

Perhaps some of the criticism regarding the Elliott/Gustafson combination stems from the performance of the No. 9 team in 2026.

Things started out promising for Elliott and company. The 2020 Cup champion won the seventh race of the campaign at Martinsville Speedway, the earliest in a season he had ever won before. Four races later, Elliott captured another victory at Texas Motor Speedway.

However, things went downhill from there as Elliott scored only one top-5 finish in the next 15 races. Elliott dropped from as high as third in the standings to eighth by the time the Chase began.

In the Chase, Elliott only led one lap throughout the 10-race period and fell back to 12th in the standings by season's end. Elliott scored 13 top-10 finishes, a career-low, and tied his career-low for average finish at 15.1.

Elliott only scored eight top-5 finishes during the 2026 season, the second-lowest in his career. His lowest was seven top fives in 2023, a year where he missed six races.

What started out as a strong year for Elliott turned into a difficult one as the season carried on.

articles.title: Former WWE star Dana Brooke has big family news after overcoming personal heartbreak and health challenges
articles.summary: Former WWE star Dana Brooke is 32 weeks pregnant with a baby boy.
articles.body: Former WWE star Dana Brooke is 32 weeks pregnant with a baby boy. The wrestler, who now competes as Ash By Elegance, shared the news on TMZ’s Inside The Ring and said her due date is January 11, 2027. Brooke reached this point after a miscarriage last year, an ICU stay in February and a Crohn’s disease diagnosis in May. Doctors still classify the pregnancy as high-risk. She says she feels better than ever anyway. The birth is planned as a C-section, and her son already has a name: Kairos.What did Dana Brooke go through before this pregnancy news?Brooke first became pregnant in August 2025, which led to her retirement announcement from TNA. Two months later she had a miscarriage. In February 2026, severe stomach pain and internal bleeding put her in the ICU. She needed three blood transfusions and was moved between three hospitals while doctors hunted for a cause.The answer came on May 6, when she was diagnosed with Crohn’s disease. It is a lifelong autoimmune condition, and Brooke now takes monthly infusions and a monthly injection. She had never been ill in her life, so the news came out of nowhere. She was also told to step back from wrestling because of inflammation in her intestines and stomach, and she admits she took it badly.At the end of May, she found out she was pregnant again. Brooke says the miscarriage taught her to wait. She had told her work, friends and parents the first time and was about to announce it publicly when everything fell apart. This time she told no one, not work, family or friends, until she passed the halfway mark. A gender reveal party followed.Brooke says “he has been a blessing, he’s been a miracle.” Her doctors told her pregnancy can steer Crohn’s toward remission, and she says that is what happened. She has had no flare-ups since the early stages, and her 32-week scan showed a thriving baby.TNA contract status and a possible return to the ringBrooke’s TNA contract expires at the end of December, and the company has left the door open for a return. She announced her retirement from TNA after that first pregnancy in 2025, but the promotion has not shut her out.She has the résumé to back a comeback. Brooke joined NXT in 2013 after competing in fitness events, and in 2015 she became the first WWE Superstar to enter the Fitness International competition at the Arnold Sports Festival. She later won the 24/7 Championship multiple times. In TNA, she captured the Knockouts title.Brooke hopes to step back into the ring one day and show her son just how tough his mom is. articles.title: Maple Leafs Have Bigger Problems Than the Standings
articles.summary: The Toronto Maple Leafs can't think about their place in the standings when there is so much to work on this season. The post Maple Leafs Have Bigger Problem...
articles.body:
The last thing the Toronto Maple Leafs want to do right now is look at the standings. Seeing themselves in last place in the Atlantic Division could do far more harm than good.

Unless the team can find some sort of motivation in seeing themselves at the bottom of the division, the only thing the Leafs need to look at is themselves.

The club just needs to work hard and focus on controlling the things they can control. Otherwise, the prospect of salvaging this season may be too much to pull off.

For now, the talk shouldn't be about making the playoffs. Yes, that's a major goal for the organization. But it shouldn't be the only thing guiding the team's performance at this point. The guiding factor should be trying to get back to the fundamentals and win hockey games.

It might sound like a cliché, but the Maple Leafs have entered a territory in which only the next game matters.

While injuries have played a major role in derailing their season, the fact is that the only thing the Leafs can actually do about it is go out there and execute. One can find all the sports adages used to help teams focus on winning.

But the bottom line is that the only game that matters is the next one. Thinking about games in the spring won't do anyone any good.

Maple Leafs Have to Dump Thoughts of Magic Fixes

From time to time, everyone wishes there was a magic button they could just push to solve everything.

That would be fantastic if it really existed. Such a magic button would make Morgan Rielly, Oliver Ekman-Larsson and Chris Tanev 10 years younger. That button would also morph Sergei Bobrovsky into the Vezina Trophy-caliber goalie he once was.

Heck, that magic button would wipe 10 years off John Tavares and restore Auston Matthews to his 60-goal form.

Alas, that button doesn't exist. And so, Maple Leafs GM John Chayka cannot afford to think that there's a single solution out there. A coaching change or a major trade won't save the season. Even if it doesn't end in a playoff appearance, turning things around this year won't happen with some incantation or ritual.

The turnaround will happen with the team avoiding the costly mistakes that doomed its six-game homestand.

Toronto Still Has Time to Turn It Around

Even at the risk of sounding like hopium, the Maple Leafs still have time to turn things around. The team has the talent and the firepower to make a run at a playoff spot.

Once in, Toronto could become a very tough out.

The clock is ticking, nonetheless. That's why the focus can't go beyond the next game or even the next shift. Teams that focus on winning each shift end up winning hockey games. Like losses, wins quickly pile up. And if rivals even stumble just a little, a hot team can make up ground in the standings.

Ultimately, the Maple Leafs don't really have much of a choice. It's either give up on the season and play out the string, even in November, or take it one game at a time and try to make a serious run at it.

articles.title: Duke hits new low in 37 years with blowout loss to Illinois

articles.body:
History has the receipts proving Duke is a basketball powerhouse . However, nobody is completely invincible.

On Tuesday, No. 5 Duke reluctantly welcomed No. 10 Illinois to the famed Cameron Indoor Stadium in Durham, North Carolina. The Illini defeated the Blue Devils 99-78. It was not only a blowout loss, but also the first of its kind in a long time for Duke, per Joe Tipton of On3Sports.com.

The last time the Blue Devils lost by more than 20 points at home was in 1989, 37 years ago, to be exact. Additionally, the Blue Devils ' 35-game winning streak at home came to an end.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Illinois came ready to play. A major factor was Andrej Stojakovic scoring a record 46 points , the most points scored by an opponent at Cameron Indoor Stadium since Grady Wallace scored 43 points for South Carolina in 1957. Despite their size and height, Duke was outrebounded by Illinois in a 54-34 win. The Illini also grabbed 18 offensive rebounds and scored 19 second-chance points.

Plus, Illinois won the battle in the paint, 48-30. They also put up 22 points off 14 Blue Devils turnovers. The Blue Devils shot 24-for-64 from the field (37.5%) and 9-for-40 from 3 (22.5%). They were also only 21-for-33 from the field and missed 12 free throws.

For Duke, freshman center Joaquim Boumtje-Boumtje led the way with 17 points and five rebounds. Senior guard Caleb Foster added 15 points and six rebounds. Second-year guard/forward Sebastian Wilkins added 10 points.

The Blue Devils are now 3-2. They enter the season trying to shake off an Elite Eight exit to UConn after being the No. 1 seed. On Saturday, the Blue Devils will play against Utah in Pittsburgh.

Hamilton shot 7 of 14 from the floor, 8 of 10 from the free-throw line and made both 3-point attempts. Jamil Miller scored 16 points and grabbed 10 rebounds for Eastern Washington. Marquardt chipped in with with 13 points and eight rebounds. Scherer scored eight.

Alec Anigbata scored 16 points and grabbed 10 rebounds to lead Utah (3-1). Trey Campbell added 15 points. Jackson Holcombe finished with 13 points, nine rebounds and four assists.

The Kansas City Chiefs reportedly bought in former Philadelphia Eagles offensive lineman Fred Johnson for a workout on Tuesday after he was released by the Eagles back on Nov. 13.

After Johnson cleared waivers on Monday he was free to sign with any team. And it appears that a decision has been made rather quickly, as he has now signed with Kansas City.

Chiefs Sign Former Eagles Offensive Lineman Fred Johnson

The news was also released onto the Chiefs' official website.

"John FitzPatrick (TE), E.J. Smith (RB), Fred Johnson (T) signed to the Practice Squad. Jacob De Jesus (WR), Bub Means (WR), Cole Christiansen (LB) Practice Squad contracts terminated." The team's official site posted on Nov. 17.

Will Fred Johnson Suit Up For the Chiefs This Weekend?

The move to add Johnson to the practice squad rather than the active roster likely signals the team's uncertainty about the playing statuses of right tackle Jaylon Moore and guard Trey Smith, who are dealing with an ankle injury and a concussion respectively.

If both are good to for Week 11, it's less likely that the Chiefs will see Johnson either activated for game-day or possibly full-on elevated to the 53-man roster.

If the pair are both ruled out, there is a far better likelihood that Kansas City will require his services in some form come this weekend's game hosting the Arizona Cardinals.

Johnson joins a thin practice squad offensive line setup that currently sports 2024 undrafted free agent tackle Ethan Driskell and rookie UDFA center Pete Nygra as the only representatives of the unit.

articles.title: Spurs' Dylan Harper injured late in Tuesday night's loss to Detroit
articles.summary: The guard headed to the locker room with 53.6 seconds left after slipping on the court. He finished with 20 points, four rebounds and two assists in the loss...
articles.body:
Dynamic Spurs guard Dylan Harper suffered an injury late in Tuesday night's 105-93 loss to Detroit at the Frost Bank Center.

Harper headed to the locker room aided by teammate Keldon Johnson and a team staffer after slipping and landing awkwardly on the court while attempting to catch a pass from Stephon Castle with 53.6 seconds left. He grabbed at his left groin and hip area while in visible pain before Spurs star Victor Wembanyama rushed over to check on him.

There was no word from the Spurs (12-3) after the game about the extent of the injury. It also wasn't immediately known if a wet spot on the floor caused Harper to go down.

"It just looked like he slipped, obviously, so hoping for the best, but don't know anything yet," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said.

Harper finished with 20 points on 8-of-14 shooting (0 of 4 from 3-point range), four rebounds and two assists in 35 minutes.

Wembanyama said it was a "terrible feeling, terrible sight" to see the 20-year-old New Jersey native in pain.

"I know as much as you guys, so I hope he's fine," said Wembanyama, who had 25 points and 18 rebounds in the loss, which snapped the Spurs' 12-game winning streak. "I'll check on him today. But, yeah, I just hate this. I don't know how else I can say this."

Harper entered the game averaging 18.3 points on 50% shooting from the field and 34.0% from 3-point range to go along with 5.5 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.0 steals in 31.5 minutes. He was fresh off scoring a career-high 31 points in a 110-102 victory at Utah on Sunday afternoon.

"He's really fit into this role where we can trust him and we know we can go to him because he's relentless for defenses," Wembanyama said. "They can't rest when he's on the court because he's so able to attack the rim and so smart with his body. So he's just a reliable guy."

Several NBA stars have suffered injuries this season, but the Spurs have yet to have a major setback. That could change, though, after Harper's ugly mishap.

"At certain parts of (last) season we didn't have certain guys and what made us go is we were able to kind of cover for guys when they were out," Spurs guard De'Aaron Fox said. "So, right now, it looks like we might have to do that again."

articles.title: BeatLine Sports Shows Why Sports Media Should Take AI More Seriously

articles.body:
If you haven't heard the news, artificial intelligence is getting into the content space. From images and videos to songs that have landed on the charts, AI-crafted content is becoming more accepted by the minute.

Yesterday, sports media went on the defensive when BeatLine Sports surfaced with its AI-driven content model and podcast lineup. Every team, every angle, all created through generative AI. The latest headlines and discussions are being produced. But they still come with the familiar AI-related concerns about fact-checking.

For the first time, however, sports media has a tangible example of how AI can attract an audience through podcasting. The technology is here, and it arrived quicker than many expected. But why is this moment being treated as a joke by many in the industry?

There seems to be a common belief among many in the sports media space that AI will never replace them. How could something without a human touch, thought or human experience connect with human emotion? We once thought the idea of people flying to destinations was a pipe dream. Remember your first computer? Now, it's in your pocket.

Time allows technology to evolve. People and society evolve with it. We're more on the go than ever before because the pace of business is no longer confined to the hours of nine to five. There's also more competition for content, along with more outlets for people to seek out and consume information and entertainment.

That's why I had to laugh a little yesterday. Not only while sampling the content provided by BeatLine Sports but also while watching the reaction to it from people across sports media . Yes, the content is choppy . Names are mispronounced , and the delivery lacks the natural cadence of an actual human being.

It's AI slop, fitting the definition. But this is the first major attempt. Every new piece of technology has to start somewhere.

The cost of doing business in media is expensive, and every company is looking for models that can produce more content with less overhead. With technology, the goal is to build on the initial product and figure out what's next. It's about investing instead of cutting.

At the heart of BeatLine Sports is Ibunl Jaif Farabi . He reportedly moved to the United States after earning a degree in electrical and electronics engineering from Rajshahi University of Engineering and Technology. According to reports, he founded AI999x, an independent AI lab that develops small, fast scientific AI models capable of running on any device without an internet connection, an account or information being sent elsewhere.

That's a pretty cool description for an about page, if you ask me.

If you trust that this man is real, his verified X account has been very active over the past couple of days. He claims BeatLine Sports content isn't created through prompts at all. Farabi says he's generating 2,000 podcasts using custom-created models and agents, with each publishing one or two episodes per day automatically and at no cost. He also claims his models are in the early stages of a "recursive self-improving system," in which everything he generates will improve exponentially.

His mission : Create a podcast for every sports team in the world. Farabi says, "Compete or perish."

Will BeatLine Sports put people out of work tomorrow? Next week? In a year? Likely not.

The bigger concern is the attempt itself.

A recent Pew Research Center study showed that 49% of Americans reported using AI chatbots. That's up from 33% just two years ago. The top reason people use an AI chatbot is to search for information. The third-highest reason? Fun or entertainment.

The Sounds Profitable Podcast Landscape 2026 report shows that 26% of those surveyed find it acceptable for AI to produce entirely AI-generated audio or video content. Another 22% find AI-generated hosts or talent acceptable.

In five years, as AI evolves, how much further will the technology advance, and how much will audience acceptance grow alongside it?

Sports media shouldn't be so quick to dance on the grave of the first serious AI-generated sports podcast model. Instead, the industry should be paying close attention to what just happened and asking what comes next.

BeatLine Sports might not be the threat that puts people out of work tomorrow. Its content might be clunky, its delivery might lack personality, and its reporting might require plenty of human oversight. But none of that should distract from the fact that someone just demonstrated a willingness to build an automated content operation capable of producing thousands of sports podcasts at little to no cost.

The first version of anything rarely represents its final form. Technology will improve. Voices will become more natural. Content will become more sophisticated. And the audience that once laughed at the idea of listening to an AI-generated sports podcast might eventually become comfortable doing so.

The biggest mistake sports media can make is confusing today's limitations with tomorrow's possibilities. BeatLine Sports might ultimately fail. It might disappear as quickly as it arrived. But the idea behind it isn't going away. If the reaction from sports media is to laugh, dismiss it and move on, don't be surprised when the next version arrives with fewer flaws, a bigger audience and a much more sustainable business model.

That should be the warning. Not that AI is ready to replace sports media, but that sports media better be ready for what AI is becoming.

articles.title: Awkward Jim Harbaugh-Justin Herbert Moment Adds Weird Vibe To Chargers Win
articles.summary: It took nine games, but the Los Angeles Chargers got their first win of the 2026 regular season on Monday night against the Baltimore Ravens. A 1-8 record is...
articles.body:
It took nine games, but the Los Angeles Chargers got their first win of the 2026 regular season on Monday night against the Baltimore Ravens. A 1-8 record is not much to celebrate, and an awkward moment in the locker room after the game between head coach Jim Harbaugh and quarterback Justin Herbert just gave the whole thing a very weird vibe.

In a video shared on social media which can be viewed here, Harbaugh congratulated the team for the win and then implored everyone to give each other a high five. The camera catches Harbaugh and Herbert exchanging a high five where the signal caller did not look all that enthused as he lightly exchanged a high five with his head coach.

Some on social media saw the moment as evidence that Herbert doesn't like Harbaugh or that he doesn't have a good attitude. Others defended Herbert, asking whether he should have been doing back flips for their first win of the season. It's probably just a moment that got blown way out of proportion but when a team has had as terrible a season as the Chargers, every single little moment is going to be scrutinized whether it is fair or not.

To give Herbert the benefit of the doubt, it has been a brutal season. He probably doesn't want to be celebrating too hard when his team is just having a completely embarrassing year. Plus, Herbert has always been fairly mild-mannered and reserved. Mina Kimes wrote a whole profile about Herbert years ago for ESPN which delved into how he is an introvert and just simply isn't the big personality that many people expect an NFL quarterback to be.

Herbert and Harbaugh really do not mix on paper

That is what makes the Herbert-Harbaugh pairing so interesting on paper. Harbaugh is loud, bombastic, and prone to outbursts. Herbert is serene, cool, and supremely understated. It wouldn't seem like the two would work together well but sometimes opposites attract in relationships.

The last two seasons the two seemed to work together quite well as the team went 11-6 and made the playoffs each season. Maybe the addition of offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel is what threw things off a bit but Herbert has remained steadfast in his support of his offensive playcaller .

Maybe the moment in the locker room is evidence of Herbert showing his displeasure with his head coach, or maybe it's just how Herbert is. He and Harbaugh are completely different personality-wise so most likely it is just a case of two very different people sharing a bit of an awkward moment which wouldn't even be blinked at if the team was 8-1 rather than 1-8.

articles.title: Tennessee held Michigan State to a historic nine made shots in win
articles.summary: Michigan State made just nine shots in the loss to Tennessee, a historically bad night that had Tom Izzo calling it an "all-time low"
articles.body:
Tennessee changed the narrative on its early season concerns with a statement win against Michigan State , and it did so with a historic defensive performance.

In the 61-46 Volunteers win, Michigan State made just nine shots, its fewest in a game over 30 years, according to the ESPN broadcast, in what was one of the roughest shooting nights in Tom Izzo's entire tenure. It was also the fewest made shots by any Division I team since January 2024, according to ESPN Insights .

"We got punched in the mouth tonight," Izzo said postgame.

It started off a defensive battle, with Tennessee holding a 27-25 lead at halftime after the Spartans made six shots in the opening frame. But out of halftime, the clamps were on Sparty.

In the second half, Michigan State went 3-for-26 from the field. The Spartans didn't make a shot until five minutes into the half, and then made another nearly four minutes later.

See who dominates Nielsen's list of top college basketball fan bases

Michigan State then went seven minutes without making a shot, getting its final field goal with four minutes left in the game. In the final 11 minutes, the Spartans 1-for-13 from the field, resulting in the 9-for-50 (18%) night with a 4-for-19 (21.1%) mark from 3-point land, with Izzo calling it an "an all-time low."

That also includes star Jeremy Fears Jr. not making a single shot on the night.

The only reason Michigan State stayed in the game for the majority of the second half was getting to the foul line. In total, Michigan State's 46 points came from the free throw line, with Fears getting all 16 of his points from the charity stripe.

It was an epic and signature defensive performance for Rick Barnes, who is now a perfect 7-0 at home against teams in the top five of the Associated Press poll. With some big performances from Miles Rubin and Dewayne Brown, the Volunteers have gotten back on course to assert themselves as a contender.

articles.title: Prep basketball roundup: Sherman Oaks Notre Dame holds off Palisades in high-scoring opener
articles.summary: Zion Lanier scored 26 points for Notre Dame in 94-87 win over defending City Section champion Palisades.
articles.body:
As opening games go in high school basketball, Tuesday night's matchup between preseason No. 2-ranked Sherman Oaks Notre Dame and No. 12 Palisades produced a game that proved both teams are headed for lots of victories this season.

In the end, Notre Dame, despite playing much of the second half without standout guard NaVorro Bowman (shoulder injury) held on for a 94-87 victory. The teams combined to have nine players score in double figures and make 26 threes.

Junior guard Zion Lanier, who has been earning rave reviews at Notre Dame practices from coach Matt Sargeant, scored a career-high 26 points. "I had a meeting before the season with coach," he said. "I had to adjust to a new role and get out of my shell."

Bowman had 18 points before leaving the game in the third quarter. His arm was in a sling. Ilan Nikolov made four threes in the third quarter and finished with 18 points. Sophomore Nico Mecilli came off the bench to score a career-high 16 points and Josiah Nance had 14 points. Notre Dame made 15 threes.

Palisades, which was down 18 points at halftime, made a determined second-half comeback and left little doubt that it will be an overwhelming favorite to defend its City Section Open Division title. Sophomore guard Phil Reed scored 15 of his 26 points in third quarter. EJ Popola had 20 points, OJ Popola 18 and Jack Levey 17.

The Dolphins have aspirations of challenging top Southern Section teams, and Tuesday's performance sent a clear message they can do it. They play St. Francis on Saturday.

"We dug ourselves a hole," Palisades coach Jeff Bryant said. "We made proper adjustments and fought back in the second half and came up short. That was a shootout. That's why we schedule these games to see where we're at."

St. John Bosco 83, Newport Harbor 27: David Conerly led the way with 16 points and Chace Patterson had 14 points.

Milken 79, St. Monica 63: Grayson Coleman started his senior season with a 35-point performance.

Harvard-Westlake 93, St. Genevieve 35: Alex Floyd scored 20 points, Nairobi Ebi 17 and Pierce Thompson 15 for the Wolverines, who also received seven assists from Cole Holden.

Anaheim Canyon 78, South Torrance 50: Tolu Akomolafe made seven threes and finished with 27 points.

Damien 81, Torrance 39: Zaire Rasshan had 22 points for Damien (2-0).

Etiwanda 64, Rancho Verde 45: Devin Mitchell had 34 points for the Eagles.

Sherman Oaks Notre Dame 73, Palisades 29: Sophomores Alexa Castillo (15 points) and Elsie Hodge (12 points) led the Knights. Freshman Cali Bowman scored 12 points in her high school debut. She's the sister of boys' star NaVorro Bowman.

Oaks Christian 74, Oxnard 47: Presley Kushner scored 28 points and Bonita Liu added 23 points.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: AFC Playoff Picture: How standings, playoff odds look after Bengals blowout, Drake Maye injury
articles.summary: As the NFL season passes the halfway point, the AFC playoff teams are starting to take hold of their positions. There are seven spots in the AFC playoffs, an...
articles.body:
As the NFL season passes the halfway point, the AFC playoff teams are starting to take hold of their positions. There are seven spots in the AFC playoffs, and it would not be a shocker if the teams that currently own those positions would finish the season as postseason teams.

The Buffalo Bills have the best record in the AFC , and they are rolling with an 8-1 record. The Bills have been motivated all season under first-year head coach Joe Brady. The Bills were angry a year ago when they lost their grip on the division and the New England Patriots took advantage of a fourth-place schedule and stole it from them. They appear to be quite secure in their position as they have a 3.5-game lead over the Pats (5-5), who have lost two in a row and saw QB Drake Maye go down with an ankle injury.

The Bills are plus-110 to emerge with the No. 1 seed in the AFC playoffs, according to DraftKings. The Bills are the only team likely to make the playoffs from the AFC East. The Patriots still have a chance, but they will be sending Tommy DeVito out to lead the attack, and he struggled badly after taking over for Maye in the Week 10 loss to the Detroit Lions.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

MVP candidate Joe Burrow is driving the Bengals

The Cincinnati Bengals (7-2) are on a major roll this season, and much of that is due to the health and dominance of QB Joe Burrow. The Bengals have won five games in a row, and Burrow has thrown for 2,795 yards with 27 TD passes and 6 interceptions. Based on his performance in the winning streak, Burrow looks unstoppable at this point. The Bengals are plus-600 to finish with the No. 1 seed in the AFC.

As dominant and exciting as the Bills and Bengals have been through the first half of the season, the Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2) have been nearly as good. The Jaguars have a 4.0-game lead over the Houston Texans (3-6) and they appear to be rolling to the AFC South title. Trevor Lawrence has reached elite status in the NFL, and he is having a brilliant year for head coach Liam Coen. Lawrence has completed 171 of 259 passes for 2,284 yards with a razor-sharp 21-5 TD-interception ratio.

The Jaguars are listed at plus-500 to end up with the No. 1 seed in the AFC playoffs.

The Bills, Bengals and Jaguars appear to have the best route to the playoffs and the top seed in the AFC. However, the Kansas City Chiefs and the Denver Broncos can't be counted out in the AFC West. Both teams are well on their way to making the playoffs and it's just a question of which of these 7-2 teams is going to emerge with the AFC West crown.

The Chiefs are demonstrating that last year's 6-11 finish was basically just a fluke The Chiefs have returned to excellent form and there is always confidence when Patrick Mahomes has the ball in his hands in a close game. The Chiefs are listed as minus-12500 to make the playoffs and plus-550 to earn the No. 1 seed in the AFC.

Broncos have easier closing schedule than Chiefs

The Broncos appear to have a better shot at winning the AFC West crown over the Chiefs because their closing schedule is much easier. They play the Raiders twice, the Dolphins, the Jets and the Chargers, while the Chiefs have challenging games against the Bills, Rams and Bengals in consecutive weeks and another tough game against the 49ers. The Broncos are minus-8000 to make the AFC playoffs and plus-380 to take the No. 1 seed.

The Pittsburgh Steelers (6-3) and the surprising Cleveland Browns (6-4) are both in positions to take the final two seeds in the AFC playoffs. The Steelers suffered a 38-18 loss to the Bengals in Week 10, but head coach Mike McCarthy and QB Aaron Rodgers have no reason to panic. The Steelers are listed at minus-290 to make the playoffs. Their closing schedule features tough games against Denver and Jacksonville and winnable games against Philadelphia, Baltimore (2), Carolina and Tennessee.

The Browns currently have the No. 7 and final seed in the AFC playoffs. They have a 1.0-game lead over the Patriots, and while history says that it will be difficult for Cleveland to hold on to that playoff spot, first-year head coach Todd Monken has this team believing in itself even though this team is devoid of stars. The Browns are minus-130 to make the playoffs.

The Browns have been depending on Deshaun Watson at quarterback, and he has thrown for 2,118 yards and 7 TDs. He has also demonstrated that he can run away from pass rushers. He has 266 rushing yards and 2 TDs. The Browns are getting a lift from tight end Harold Fanin Jr. He has caught 44 passes for 544 yards and 4 TDs.

The struggling Patriots are the closest team that is out of the AFC playoff structure to gaining a position, but the absence of Maye means it is a major long shot Mike Vrabel's team to make the playoffs.

If the Browns are going to fall apart, it would seem that the Las Vegas Raiders or the Texans have the best shot at making a run at the postseason. The Raiders (4-6) have some winnable games against the Browns, Chargers, Titans and Cardinals, but their trade of QB Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings may have hurt their chances for success.

The Texans were expected to battle the Jaguars for the division title because they have a potentially dominant defense. They would suddenly have to hit their stride in order to make a run, but that seems unlikely because of the way DeMeco Ryans' team has played to this point.

articles.title: Pro athletes clamor for 'Grand Theft Auto VI' release, but they insist their day jobs come first
articles.summary: LOS ANGELES (AP) — When “Grand Theft Auto VI” finally drops this week, professional athletes across the globe will immediately begin stealing cars, running f...
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — When "Grand Theft Auto VI" finally drops this week, professional athletes across the globe will immediately begin stealing cars, running from the cops and causing every manner of virtual mayhem under the Vice City sun.

The love affair between pro athletes and video games has been strong for decades now, and the most anticipated game release in over a decade is certain to cause sleep-deprived nights and create mostly friendly competition across locker rooms and clubhouses — even if everybody insists they won't let it be a distraction from their day jobs.

"I told my mom she might not hear from me for a couple of days," Los Angeles Rams receiver Tutu Atwell said with a grin.

Atwell is an avid gamer and a Miami native who has been playing the GTA series since childhood, so the release of this iteration set in a fictional Florida is monumental. He preordered "GTA VI" to appear on his console right at midnight — and he even looked into changing his region setting to New Zealand so he could get the game 21 hours earlier, but ultimately decided it wasn't worth the hassle.

"We've been waiting for this one for a long, long time," Atwell said. "You know it's going to be a big one."

Pro athletes become avid gamers for obvious reasons: They're nearly all competition junkies with plenty of money and thousands of hours of free time to game after practices, in road hotels and throughout their offseasons.

Athletes from Kyler Murray to Karl-Anthony Towns have amassed large followings on the livestreaming platform Twitch, playing games like the NBA 2K and Madden titles or first-person shooters like "Fortnite" and "Call of Duty" before tens of thousands of viewers. Formula 1 champions Max Verstappen and Lando Norris often seem just as enthusiastic about simulated racing as the real thing. Some athletes even become elite gamers: Lakers superstar Luka Doncic, for instance, was a top-500 player in the tank role on "Overwatch 2" two years ago.

But no series dazzles a wider spectrum of the gaming public than GTA — and its long absence from the market only made these athletes hungrier.

Rockstar Games released "GTA V" in 2013, when a large chunk of the world's current pro athletes were adolescents, and the release of "GTA VI" has been tantalizingly delayed for several years.

Several weeks ago, Houston Rockets center Steven Adams predicted a seismic disruption to all sports when the game finally arrived.

"You guys should anticipate November, the performance of the league, league-wide ... GTA is dropping," Adams said. "So look at NFL, look at all the leagues and watch them plummet, mate. Just for the month of November, performance is going to go down. It should come back up, though. Most of the boys will get it done, hopefully they finish the game. Coaching as well, by the way. The coaching and scouts are going to be horrendous, mate. Just for November, but it should bounce back in December, hopefully. Should be good."

Whether he was joking or not, Adams nonetheless set off rampant chatter about what the game's release will mean for athlete and workplace productivity.

When asked directly, most high-level athletes say they're too serious about sports to develop a severe case of GTA Flu. That's the term coined in 2013 when untold thousands of gamers took days off work to dive headfirst into San Andreas, the game's fictionalized version of Southern California.

Los Angeles Rams left guard Steve Avila doesn't expect athletes to shirk their primary duties, but he knows the game will still affect plenty of pros in more subtle ways.

"I think a lot of athletes are responsible," Avila said. "But if you could check guys' sleep scores ... I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down, for sure."

Avila is a big admirer of Rockstar's artistic ambitions along with GTA's famously frenetic game play. He had never been to California before he played "Grand Theft Auto," so he and his friends have been repeatedly surprised in recent years to see the real versions of Los Angeles-area landmarks they already recognized from speeding past them in a stolen car while being chased by virtual cops.

The Rams players are among the fortunate few athletes who are on their bye week when the game is released — and Avila is even on injured reserve, although he laughingly insists his rehab work will supersede GTA.

Jets running back Breece Hall echoes both Avila's enthusiasm for the game and his belief the day job comes first. Hall's mother only allowed him to play sports video games, so he has been waiting a decade for the chance to immerse himself in a chapter of the GTA franchise.

"Yeah, definitely getting the film done early, and then spending the extra hour or two on the game," Hall said. "But you've got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun."

Phoenix Suns guard Devin Booker is an inveterate gamer who travels with a gaming laptop and has played "Grand Theft Auto" since before multiplayer options were available. The five-time NBA All-Star loves to "go in there and just be reckless," he said with a laugh.

Like Atwell, Booker has already preordered "GTA VI."

The game is a childhood throwback for younger pros like Anaheim Ducks star Leo Carlsson, who played earlier versions for untold hours as a kid in Sweden. He'll dive into it when the Ducks return from a road trip — and like many athletes, he's eagerly anticipating the game's multiplayer component, which isn't expected to be available until 2027.

"I love playing with teammates," Carlsson said. "If they dropped (GTA) in the summer, it would probably take over huge time in our life."

"GTA VI" is set in a chimerical Florida called Leonida, which contains Vice City – the franchise's stand-in for Miami .

And the NBA's Miami Heat are at the epicenter of the release when they hold "A Night in Vice City" on Wednesday.

The Heat have topped Kaseya Center with a "Vice City" neon sign as an advertisement for the game, and they'll wear themed alternate uniforms when they face Milwaukee on a special court. The entire night in downtown Miami will have a GTA theme.

"It's a big thing because growing up as a kid, we all were on 'Grand Theft Auto,'" Heat forward Bobby Portis said. "It's been like a buildup, and everybody's been asking when this was going to come out. Just so happy that we're here in Miami when it does. Definitely an honor to be able to grace the Vice City and be a part of history."

Heat forward Keshad Johnson said he played the GTA franchise "all my life growing up. It's been so long since the last one came out. But for there to be a new one and to be a part of it, that's gonna be fire. That's gonna be dope. … I've seen the jerseys. Elite."

AP Basketball Writer Tim Reynolds in Miami and AP Sports Writers Dennis Waszak Jr. in New York, Pat Graham in Denver and David Brandt in Phoenix contributed to this report.
