articles.body:
SEATTLE (AP) — LeJuan Watts came off the bench to score 17 points and Washington cruised to a 96-59 victory over Division II's Simon Fraser on Tuesday night.

Watts sank 8 of 10 shots from the floor with a 3-pointer and added five rebounds and three assists for the Huskies (3-0), who scheduled the Red Leafs at the last minute after their game against the Utes in Utah was postponed when the FAA grounded all flights on Nov. 13.

Steele Venters finished with 14 points for Washington, Wesley Yates III scored 13 and reserve Wini Braga added 12.

Watts scored 13 points in the first half, making all six of his shots, including the 3-pointer, to help Washington take a 56-29 lead into the break by shooting 74% from the floor.

Yates had 10 first-half points for the Huskies, who took their first double-digit lead at 19-8 with 14:32 remaining. The advantage grew to 20 on a three-point play by Lathan Sommerville that made it 49-29 with 2:49 left.

Washington pushed the lead above 30 at 76-44 on a 3-pointer by Braga with 10:18 left to play.

Reserve Chris Lee led the Red Leafs, a Division II school from British Columbia, with 14 points and six boards. Mikyle Malabuyoc scored 11.

The Huskies shot 55% from the floor but made only 14 of 38 from 3-point range and 10 of 19 at the free-throw line. The Huskies dominated the boards 47-22 with 18 coming at the offensive end, leading to 21 second-chance points.

Washington will host Utah Tech on Thursday.

articles.title: Aljamain Sterling Reveals Umar Nurmagomedov’s Alleged Role in Yas Hilton Hotel Brawl With Merab Dvalishvili
articles.summary: Aljamain Sterling claims Umar Nurmagomedov attacked Merab Dvalishvili off-camera during the Yas Hilton Hotel brawl.
articles.body:
The controversy surrounding the altercation at the Yas Hilton Hotel during RAF Abu Dhabi has taken another unexpected turn. The incident involved Merab Dvalishvili and Saba Lazishvili, who were confronted by Usman Nurmagomedov and members of his Dagestani entourage.

Videos circulating online captured the moment the PFL champion approached Dvalishvili and slapped the Georgian fighter, setting off a mass brawl involving multiple individuals. Authorities subsequently detained all 10 people involved, with the group spending nearly 48 hours in custody.

Dvalishvili and Lazishvili eventually walked free after reportedly receiving a $14,000 fine without any jail time. The outcome was harsher for the Dagestani contingent. Eight individuals, including Nurmagomedov, were reportedly handed six-month prison sentences , alongside an $82,000 fine and deportation orders to be enforced after their prison terms.

Following a revision of the original ruling, all eight convicted Dagestanis have now been released , according to an update shared by the Abu Dhabi Criminal Court on X. While this development could appear to bring the legal proceedings to a close, the fallout from the hotel brawl may not be over just yet.

Dvalishvili's teammate and former UFC bantamweight champion, Aljamain Sterling, has revealed more harrowing details of the attack that were not captured on tape. First, Aljo slammed the Dagestani contingent for a cowardly attack.

In an interview with ESPN , Sterling did not hold back when discussing the incident, saying, "I wish I was there—me and the other boys—to see if they would have kept that same energy because they have this M.O. for doing this type of thing."

He further questioned the manner in which the Dagestani group confronted Dvalishvili, adding, "They don't approach guys one-on-one, and I would have respected Usman if he would have done that, or established he has a problem, or him slapping Merab and establishing he had a problem. But to do that with a group of guys, it's just soft. It's just animalistic behavior."

However, Sterling's biggest allegation concerned what happened after the cameras stopped recording. He claimed that Umar Nurmagomedov, who was absent from the viral footage circulating online, joined the altercation later and attacked Dvalishvili. Sterling said, "Umar was nowhere to be found, but after the camera turns off, Umar then comes up and punches Merab in the face."

The former champion also questioned Umar Nurmagomedov's conduct during the aftermath of the initial confrontation, stating, "It looked like he was going to de-escalate the situation because this was after everything kind of settled down. What about this is respectable?"

Sterling went on to describe the alleged off-camera events as particularly disturbing. He concluded, "I could have let the first clip that was shown on video go, but after I heard about everything that happened afterward — nah. To Umar walking up and doing what he did. Then them holding down Saba — pinning his arms so they could stomp his head. I think that's attempted murder."

These allegations also align with Dvalishvili's previous account of the incident on The Ariel Helwani Show. The Georgian fighter claimed that the 30-year-old bantamweight attacked him after the initial confrontation and attributed his injuries, including multiple cuts and lacerations, to the events that unfolded once the cameras were off.

Interestingly, despite the alleged severity of the incident, Dvalishvili requested the release of the men who were imprisoned over the brawl. However, Sterling's latest allegations raise further questions about what transpired inside the hotel and whether the initial footage captured the full extent of the violence.

articles.title: Bonkers Cutter Gauthier stats prove he is untouchable right now
articles.summary: The Anaheim Ducks had a messy offseason that threatened to end their contention window before it began. So far this season, though, they have remained a comp...
articles.body:
The Anaheim Ducks had a messy offseason that threatened to end their contention window before it began. So far this season, though, they have remained a competitive team. One major reason for this is star forward Cutter Gauthier .

Gauthier may be the hottest player in the league right now. On Tuesday, he scored his fourth hat trick in nine games in a chaotic loss to the St. Louis Blues. He made history as a result, becoming the first player in league history with four hat tricks in a calendar month, via Sportsnet Stats. But the extent of his run has gone even further than that.

" Cutter Gauthier has scored 17 goals in November. That's more than the Boston Bruins, Detroit Red Wings, Columbus Blue Jackets, Buffalo Sabres, Calgary Flames, Pittsburgh Penguins, Toronto Maple Leafs or Seattle Kraken have scored in November," Associated Press reporter Greg Beacham noted on Tuesday night.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Gauthier has scored in each of his last 10 games. The last time he went without a goal was October 27 against the Vancouver Canucks. He now has 21 goals and 29 points on the season following the loss to the Blues.

The Ducks star began his incredible run on November 1st. He scored back-to-back hat tricks to begin the month. His third hat trick of the month came on November 8 against the Pittsburgh Penguins.

The Ducks still have six games remaining in the month of November. There is a chance the 22-year-old Gauthier can improve on his already incredible performance. We'll see if he can make it five hat tricks on the month when Anaheim takes on the Colorado Avalanche on Thursday.

articles.title: Cade Cunningham makes a bold claim after leading the Pistons in snapping the Spurs' streak
articles.summary: Cade Cunningham wants everyone to know the Pistons are never backing down from a challenge.
articles.body:
Heading into Tuesday's game between the Detroit Pistons and the San Antonio Spurs , the latter were the overwhelming favorites. The Pistons faced a tough game, especially without Duncan Robinson.

However, the Pistons shocked the world by taking control and winning. They snapped the Spurs ' 12-game winning streak, and Cade Cunningham was at the center of it all.

Cade Cunningham cements the Pistons as a top team once again

As one of the best point guards in the NBA, Cunningham has proven to be a fantastic player for the Pistons. He has been their leader for a while now, and he is delivering on his potential from being drafted first overall in 2021.

Since then, the Pistons have gone through all kinds of struggles, but also some solid successes. They were the first seed in the Eastern Conference in the 2025-26 season, but their early exit from the Playoffs has led to doubts. With this performance against the Spurs, the doubters were silenced.

Cunningham has affirmed that the Pistons are ready for the team to hit another level. They are ready to prove that they are still one of the best teams in the league, and they are ready to go toe-to-toe with the top teams like the Spurs.

"It was a group effort; everybody had to bring it. I like my guys; we do this together every day. We love basketball; we all come from grit, to get to this point... Nobody in that locker room has fear in their heart for anybody," Cunningham said on the NBC broadcast after the big win .

Winning against a team like the Spurs is a big achievement, and Cunningham was key to that. However, he is the first one to credit his team for helping him beat the Spurs, one of the toughest tasks any team has ths season.

articles.title: Captian Connor Bedard injured in the Chicago Blackhawks’ 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs
articles.summary: Chicago Blackhawks star center and captain Connor Bedard suffered what appeared to be a right hand, arm or shoulder injury in the third period of Tuesday’s 6...
articles.body:
Chicago Blackhawks star center and captain Connor Bedard suffered what appeared to be a right hand, arm or shoulder injury in the third period of Tuesday's 6-3 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs at the United Center. Coach Jeff Blashill said the 21-year-old will undergo testing on Wednesday.

Bedard was seen postgame without a sling or any additional support on his right arm.

"I hate to comment further until I know more, I think everybody saw it," Blashill said. "I don't know what that means, though."

On a faceoff 54 seconds into the third period, forward Nick Paul's swipe hit Bedard in the right hand . The captain was clearly frustrated, slamming his stick as he skated directly to the locker room. He didn't move his right arm on his way to the back and didn't return to the game.

The captain had a similar-looking injury last season in a road game against the St. Louis Blues. On a last-second faceoff, center Brayden Schenn lifted his stick under Bedard's right arm, causing the Hawks' star to leave the ice in visible pain. That right shoulder injury kept him out for 12 games, and in that stretch the Hawks went 5-6-1.

In July, Bedard injured his left shoulder during offseason practice in Vancouver, British Columbia. He slipped and crashed into the boards, and skated off the ice clutching his left arm. He had surgery on the shoulder, causing him to miss four months of action — including all of training camp and the first six games of this season.

Bedard has dealt with long-term injuries in three of his four NHL seasons since being selected No. 1 in the 2023 draft. He fractured his jaw in 2023-24, his Calder Trophy-winning rookie season, and missed 14 games. He played all 82 games in 2024-25.

The center has scored a team-leading 18 points this season (seven goals, 11 assists), including a second-period goal against the Leafs. In 234 career games, he has scored 221 points (82 goals, 139 assists).

Bedard's absence briefly took the air out of what was the Hawks' best offensive performance of the season. Struggling Maple Leafs goaltender Sergei Bobrovsky couldn't stop the high-octane home team, as he saw a first-period shutout turn into "Chelsea Dagger" on repeat.

Frank Nazar and company rallied the troops and didn't lose momentum after their captain left.

"Seeing a guy like him go down, you know he's probably not coming back for the rest of the game and guys need to step up," Nazar said. "That was a huge thing for all of us … we've got to go out and get the win for him."

The Hawks didn't have any offensive rhythm until the end of the first period. Toronto right wing Easton Cowan scored the period's lone goal at the 3 minute, 22 second mark, rebounding Auston Matthews' wrap-around attempt.

A not-so-memorable first period flowed into most of the next. Nazar continued his recent heater, scoring his third power-play goal in as many games at 13:17 to tie the game.

The end of the second period gave the crowd of 19,988 their money's worth. A calm game turned into chaos , and the teams had three back-to-back shifts that made the United Center crowd erupt.

First, Nazar sent a snipe from the right faceoff circle at 17:54 to give the Hawks a 2-1 lead. That was his fifth goal in three games, as well as his seventh in the last six.

In the second shift, Maple Leafs center Teddy Blueger floated a shot from behind the net, one that Spencer Knight accidentally bounced into his own net. No one, aside from Blashill, seemed to notice that, and a Hawks rush ensued, ending in a crowd-popping Oliver Moore sliding wrist shot. A referee stoppage corrected the mistake, confirming Blueger's goal and a 2-2 tie.

"I thought their shot went in," Blashill said. "I thought it ricocheted and went in originally, so I was looking at it the whole time. Then, we come down and score and I was still, 'oh, I don't know.'"

Bedard's lethal shot 35 seconds later gave the Hawks the lead for good as the period closed with a 3-2 lead.

"To me, that response was the word of the night," Blashill said. "After they scored, we responded, after (Bedard) got hurt, we responded. Obviously when (Bedard) went out, that can be a hard thing on a team and I thought our team handled it great. They really dug in and I thought they played extremely hard."

The third period became the Hawks' shooting practice. Maple Leafs enter John Tavares (11:09) scored a goal in the final 20 minutes, but it was sandwiched between two from Tyler Bertuzzi and an official Moore goal.

"(Bedard's) goal was huge before that, like just getting that one back, especially after you know they get that goal there, it was a swing of emotions," Moore said. "The crowd pop, I felt like it was pretty loud. I was fired up … I think the response was the word tonight from our group."

It was an entertaining affair, so it was easy to push aside the centennial game celebrations: 100 years ago to the night, the Hawks played their inaugural game against the Leafs — then the Toronto St. Patricks — in the Chicago Coliseum.

Team ambassadors including Chris Chelios, Eddie Olczyk and Pat Foley sounded the horn as part of the festivities. The team also named the three members of the 2026-27 Blackhawks Hall of Fame class: Brent Seabrook, Jeremy Roenick and Cliff Koroll.

The Hawks, again, might be without their captain for a period of time, depending on Bedard's assessment Wednesday.

"We've been through some tough moments over the course of this early part of the season, whether it's giving up late leads, giving up four-goal leads, late lead in Boston, getting our asses kicked in Carolina," Blashill said. "We talked about mental toughness this morning and it's a huge part of success in anything in life. You have to stay mentally tough in those moments when it doesn't go the right way. They did a good job and they should be proud of themselves for that."

articles.title: Gilbert Arenas claims ‘heartless’ Klay Thompson’s Megan Thee Stallion breakup led to resurgence
articles.summary: Klay Thompson is finding himself delivering at a level many fans got accustomed to during his prime with the Golden State Warriors. Earlier this year, Thomps...
articles.body:
Klay Thompson is finding himself delivering at a level many fans got accustomed to during his prime with the Golden State Warriors.

Earlier this year, Thompson ended his relationship with rapper Megan Thee Stallion, which became quite a pop culture controversy.

And given how well Thompson is playing since joining the Miami Heat, Gilbert Arenas believes the breakup has helped him find his form again.

Gilbert Arenas believes Klay Thompson is returning to form thanks to Megan Thee Stallion breakup

Speaking on The Arena show, Gilbert Arenas spoke about Klay Thompson's recent return to form from a shooting standpoint.

Arenas suggests that the nature and fallout of his recent breakup with rapper Megan Thee Stallion has somehow given him the confidence he needs to once again become the elite shooter he once was.

"One of the greatest shooters of all time not having his shot, when that's what you do for a living… Sometimes, certain type of minds need certain things," Arenas said. "I think the Megan Thee Stallion (situation), just watching someone like, 'this is the worst break-up I've ever had,' made him sleep good at night. The old Klay is back!"

"Sometimes, in the movie, that killer has a soft spot, and he's more vulnerable… He just lost his touch. When he'd seen that, and she was all distraught, he probably sat back like, 'Yeah. This is me. When they're crying at the doorstep, my shot is back!'

"I just really believe that's all it took. Looking at the phone, talking about, 'I hate your guts,' and he's thinking, 'Yeah, I'm about to have 30 tonight!' Everything is back.

"Klay is back! The killer is back! Keep shooting the ball, baby, and keep breaking hearts! You've got to add that part to it. He shoots like he's heartless! Gotta keep breaking hearts!"

This season, Thompson is averaging 15.5 points, 2.1 assists, and 1.4 rebounds, while shooting 45.1% from the field and 43.4% from beyond the arc.

Thompson has hit 50+ three-pointers in just 13 games this season, the fastest he has reached this mark at any point in his NBA career.

articles.title: Waterford heading to boys soccer CIAC final for first time since 1987
articles.summary: Goals by Brady Wiseman and Jaydev Villa, combined with 16 saves from Luke Wilson, carry Waterford past Hand.
articles.body:
DEEP RIVER - Waterford boys soccer coach Jeff Emerich was grooving when he heard "Jump" by Kris Kross hip-hopping over the Valley Regional PA at halftime of Tuesday night's CIAC Class M semifinal between his No. 1-seeded Lancers and No. 5 Daniel Hand.

Emerich knew, too, that if his boys executed a little more criss-cross on the pitch, they'd be jumping Waterford boys soccer into a state final for the first time since 1987, about five years before Chris "Mac Daddy" Kelly and Chris "Daddy Mac" Smith arrived on the scene.

Yeah, it all goes back a ways, and it's funny what stands the test of time.

This Waterford boys soccer team of 2026 is proving to be one for the ages. With a 2-0 victory over Hand on Tuesday night, in a game that showcased the breadth of their remarkable skill set, the Lancers are one step away from the first-ever boys soccer championship in Waterford history.

Brady Wiseman scored off a left-side cross from Brayden Michonski two minutes into the second half and Jaydev Villa, set up by an inexorable upfield rush by Yaman Qarqour, added insurance with 20:35 to play as Waterford improved to 19-1-1 and advances to this weekend's state championship at Trinity Health Stadium in Hartford to face No. 2 Weston, which dethroned reigning champ Tolland 1-0 in Tuesday's other Class M semi.

"It's been since 1987 since the last time we made it in, so this is our first chance to go up and compete," Emerich said. "We've never won a state title, and it's been 39 years since we've seen a chance, so we are very humbled that we are able to do this, and we continue to work, and that's the thing that makes these boys special."

The Lancers got an emotional boost on Monday when they learned goalie Luke Wilson was cleared from a concussion suffered in the ECC tournament semifinals against Bacon Academy. Wilson set the tone Tuesday night by charging out and sliding to break up a Hand scoring chance in the opening minute for the first of his 16 saves.

"I didn't even know if I was going to be able to play this game, especially last week, watching when we played Lewis Mills (in the quarterfinals), I was still nervous," Wilson said. "All I wanted to do was get back on the field."

Wilson wore a foam helmet for the first time Tuesday night. The rest was very much the same look for a Waterford team that has now scored 94 goals and allowed just 13 on the season.

The first half was fairly even, with both teams generating scoring chances. In the second half, the pitch decidedly tilted Waterford's way. Once Wiseman converted that cross from Michonski, a stiff challenge for Hand grew steeper. The Tigers, the last SCC team in the boys soccer state tourney, ended their season at 16-5-1.

"I thought our team came out and executed our game plan in the first half really, really well," said Hand coach Mike Shirley. "It was always going to be a game decided by one-versus-one moments, and we knew we had to defend them on the edges, and it was just about, 'Can we find our opportunities and put them in the back of the net before they can?'"

The Tigers could not, and with it passed their chance to return to the state finals for the first time since the grand slam championship run of 2016-2019.

Dates and times for all state soccer finals will be announced later this week.

Luke Wilson. Cleared from a concussion just one day before the game, Waterford's senior goalie opened the night with a sliding, charging stop to thwart a Hand scoring chance and punctuated the victory punching out a final shot in the final minute. Wilson had 16 saves in all.

"Kudos to Waterford because they have some extremely talented players, and they also played a quality game " - Hand coach Mike Shirley.

Scoring: (W) Brady Wiseman 42:01, (W) Jaydev Villa 60:25. Records: Daniel Hand 16-5-1; Waterford: 19-1-1.

articles.title: Greenwich holds off Ridgefield for 4th straight Class LL girls swimming title, 33rd overall
articles.summary: Alden Charette, Kensie Worden and Julia Kozma each won an individual event for Greenwich.
articles.body:
WEST HARTFORD - The Greenwich and Ridgefield girls swimming and diving programs have engaged in plenty of battles over the years, and the CIAC Class LL championship meet on Tuesday night at the Cornerstone Aquatics Center was no different.

For the Cardinals, depth turned out to be key as they captured their fourth straight Class LL title and 33rd overall in program history. Greenwich scored 924 points to second-place Ridgefield's 878.5. Amity was third with 510.5 points.

"I felt pretty confident going into this because I knew that everyone on the team has been working super hard, and I had a lot of faith in us," Greenwich junior Olivia DeVries said.

With sophomore Alden Charette's first-place finish in Class LL diving, the Cardinals won three individual events and one relay. Seniors Kensie Worden (50 freestyle, 23.59) and Julia Kozma (100 butterfly, 57.70) won gold medals, as did the opening 200 medley relay team of Charette, junior Sara Jee, Kozma and Worden (1:47.96).

Greenwich claimed 18 individual medals, including three golds, three silvers and three bronzes. DeVries claimed bronze medals in the 200 freestyle and 500 freestyle.

"I'm super proud of the team because we all have worked so hard in practice. The captains have done such a good job to keep us motivated and I'm just very proud of how hard we worked," DeVries said. "Every single swimmer made a difference, every single spot. If you were in the C final, the A final, everyone makes a difference. We are all cheering for each other, and I think that's what makes Greenwich special."

"We had some really great swims from all the girls, but especially our senior class," Greenwich coach Megan Kelly said. "I think it really means a lot to them, and to see them swim with such heart was really great."

Senior Ellison Charette was second in the 200 IM and 500 freestyle, and she was part of the second-place 200 and 400 freestyle relay teams.

"Ellison, she fought hard in both of her races. She had some really good swims. Overall, I was really, really pleased," Kelly said. "They didn't win the (200) free relay, but they went 1:35, which is All-American consideration time. That was pretty impressive."

Greenwich's second-place 200 freestyle relay finished in 1:35.79. Ridgefield's first-place relay of sophomore Zsofia Milak, senior Dalia Katra, sophomore Mary Kelly and junior Ellie Griffin swam the race in 1:35.21, which broke Ridgefield's 2022 state record of 1:35.48.

Milak had a terrific night for Ridgefield, winning individual gold medals in the 200 freestyle (1:50.20) and 100 freestyle (50.95). She was also part of the first-place 400 freestyle relay (3:32.60), along with Kelly, junior Chloe Archibald and sophomore Charlie Palmer. Kelly won the 500 freestyle in 4:59.44.

Norwalk/McMahon junior standout Emma Giafardino won gold medals in the 200 IM (2:05.71) and 100 breaststroke (1:04.71). Trumbull sophomore Noelle Ivanovich won the 100 backstroke in 57.47.

Greenwich and Ridgefield will likely be the top contenders Sunday for the State Open at Yale.

"I think across the board there were some really great swims. It was a battle though, and it's always fun to have a battle," Megan Kelly said. "We had it at FCIACs, now we've had it here, and Opens is going to be another battle. It makes it a lot more fun this way."

articles.title: No. 10 Illinois' Stojakovic goes for 46 points, sets scoring mark by opponent on Duke's home floor
articles.summary: (AP) — Over and over again, Andrej Stojakovic stared down a would-be defender, put the ball on the floor and slipped past on his way to attacking the paint.H...
articles.body:
DURHAM, N.C. (AP) — Over and over again, Andrej Stojakovic stared down a would-be defender, put the ball on the floor and slipped past on his way to attacking the paint.

He finished on fadeways and drives to the rim. Got to the foul line. And by the end, Stojakovic had not only led 10th-ranked Illinois to a surprisingly one-sided win against No. 5 Duke, but he had also scored the most points ever by an opponent in the Blue Devils' famously rowdy home gym.

The 6-foot-7 senior finished with 46 points in Tuesday night's 99-78 win, breaking a record that had stood for nearly seven decades while helping the Illini end Duke's 35-game winning streak at Cameron Indoor Stadium. It was part of a jarring overall performance by the Fighting Illini, both for Stojakovic's own brilliance and the way it left Blue Devils coach Jon Scheyer flummoxed by his team's lack of competitive fight.

"Just finding a rhythm, staying aggressive the whole time," Stojakovic said as he leaned against a wall in a cramped hall outside of Duke's visiting locker room. "My teammates believed in me from the start. I think credit to them for sticking with it.

"That's the beauty of this team. ... There's no ego on this team. and it could be anybody's night."

Maybe so, but there's no questioning whose night this really was.

The son of three-time NBA All-Star Peja Stojakovic had 20 by halftime on the way to finishing 14 of 21 from the field and 16 of 20 from the foul line. That allowed him to surpass the previous scoring record by a Duke opponent here: 43 points, set by South Carolina's Grady Wallace in February 1957.

Stojakovic also came within two points of matching Duke's Dick Groat (48 in February 1952) for the most points by any player in Cameron's nearly 87-year history.

Stojakovic dictated terms all night against Duke's defense

A week earlier, the Illini didn't respond to a hostile road environment in a loss at now-No. 9 Texas Tech . Stojakovic said the Illini treated this one as a must-win opportunity in how they prepared. That included his own homework of studying Duke's top defenders for tendencies.

Then he went out and dictated how this marquee nonconference matchup would play out.

"Honestly, that's what he is, that's who he is every day," said freshman Quentin Coleman, who had 27 points as the second half of a 1-2 punch. "He's a scorer, and when he goes down and scores, I don't think anybody can stop him. He just had one of those nights, and we just fed him the ball — and he just led us."

Incredibly, Stojakovic pumped out those points without relying on the 3-point shot (2 for 3), instead going with a mix of never-rushed offensive efficiency and a degree of old-fashioned attacking edge.

It was attacking in transition against Duke big man Patrick Ngongba II for a scooping layup. Elevating over a flat-footed Dame Sarr — Duke's top perimeter defender — to bury a first-half 3-pointer, then following moments later by getting John Blackwell backpedaling into the paint before turning to knock down a fadeaway.

"He's a great player, he got it going," Sarr said, "and I didn't stop him."

It was part of what coach Brad Underwood noted was an offensive performance without relying on the ball screens that helped free freshman guard and eventual No. 5 overall NBA draft pick Keaton Wagler for 46 points at Purdue last year. Rather, Underwood said, Stojakovic and his teammates simply "hunted matchups and opportunities."

Stojakovic offered tough-nosed plays too, like when he missed a muscled-up shot against Sarr — but outfought Sarr and Ngongba to the rebound and scored for while being fouled for a basket that had the Illinois bench roaring in approval.

"I hope he continues to like those things," Underwood said. "That's what we've been trying to get him to do. That's nasty. There's nastiness in that play, an aggression in that play."

Stojakovic's record output highlighted a concerning performance for Scheyer

Stojakovic finally checked out at the 1:22 mark with victory in hand, greeted by a rousing cheer from the orange-clad Illini fans packed into Cameron's bleachers behind the visiting bench and a hug from Underwood.

Across the court, that image was also a capper to a performance that Blackwell said had left him "in shock a little bit."

Scheyer credited Stojakovic for an "all-time" performance in Duke's first home loss since falling to rival North Carolina in March 2024 to end the regular season. But he was also critical of his own team's response in this marquee nonconference matchup.

Worse, this one came a week after Duke got pushed around against another Big Ten team in a loss to now-No. 2 Michigan State .

"All I would tell you guys is this is not the team we're going to put on the floor," Scheyer said. "The lack of competing that we did tonight and the lack of connectivity, we're going to fix and we're going to work like crazy.

"We may lose some games this year, but we're not going to lose where we don't compete."

articles.title: Raptors Lose 15th Straight To Knicks: 4 Takeaways From Eastern Conference Thriller
articles.summary: Analyzing the Knicks' 111-102 win over the Toronto Raptors at Scotiabank Arena.
articles.body:
Just two nights removed from their overtime loss on Sunday , the Toronto Raptors had a chance to set things right with a rematch against the New York Knicks . This time, to their credit, the Raptors came out firing with a 29-point first quarter that took the champs by surprise. By the end, however, it was the Knicks that overwhelmed, riding the play of their stars to win their second straight game (111-102) and 15th straight against the Raptors in particular.

As usual, Jalen Brunson led the way for New York. In 34 minutes, he finished with 31 points, five rebounds, five assists, zero steals, and one block on 45.5% shooting from the field (4-11 from three). At shooting guard, Mikal Bridges dropped 17 points, five rebounds, and one assist on 63.6% shooting from the field (2-5 from three), while center Karl-Anthony Towns dropped 16 points, 16 rebounds, eight assists, and one steal on 77.8% shooting from the field (1-2 from three).

For the Raptors, Ja'Kobe Walter led the way with 25 points, one rebound, two assists, and two steals on 60.0% shooting from the field (7-12 from three). Veteran swingman RJ Barrett , meanwhile, contributed 22 points, five rebounds, five assists, zero steals, and one block on 52.9% shooting from the field (2-8 from three). Finally, there's Scottie Barnes : 20 points, four rebounds, two assists, and two blocks on 50.0% shooting (1-2 from three).

Whether it was the support of their home crowd or the desperation of not wanting to lose to the same team in back-to-back games, the Raptors came out with a lot of energy in this game, playing with an almost desperate urgency during the early minutes of the game. Eventually, though, that urgency turned to frustration as the Knicks got increasingly comfortable and expanded their lead down the stretch.

In the grand scheme of things, this game likely won't be remembered for long, but it told us a lot about where these teams are headed going into the holiday season (NBA Christmas and Cup Finals). For the Knicks especially, it's a step in the right direction that could signal an upcoming shift in the hierarchy.

To say Mikal Bridges was struggling this season would be an understatement. He looked borderline unplayable at times, and head coach Mike Brown was facing growing calls to bench him . He started showing signs of life against the Pacers on Friday (18 points in 28 minutes), and he showed a familiar spark in today's win, finishing with 17 points, five rebounds, and one assist on 63.6% shooting from the field and 40.0% shooting from three. Bridges held a steady rhythm all game, and that's when the Knicks are at their best.

Of course, even when Bridges was at his worst offensively, he still made a positive impact on defense. Tonight, that defensive touch was massive in containing the Raptors' shooting and regularly contesting their attempts. Bridges was active on this end throughout the game, making that quiet impact even when he wasn't scoring.

It's unclear what had Bridges in such a funk to begin with, but everything is easier for the Knicks when he's making shots. By easing pressure off Brunson, spacing the floor, and punishing teams for leaving him open, it answers so many problems, and we saw how it worked out for them against the Raptors.

If there's one specific time when the Knicks are prone to elevate their game, it's the fourth quarter. Tonight, after stumbling through most of the first half, they sealed the deal with a 31-point fourth quarter that ultimately decided the game. New York's best moments came in the final three minutes, when Brunson single-handedly willed his team to victory after making a four-point play to put them up by four. Even Mikal got in on the action, delivering a dagger three with roughly 45 seconds left.

The Knicks started the season 1-6 in clutch games, but we can assume that was an outlier now. As we were reminded today, this team is loaded with players who are not afraid of the moment. When the pressure was highest, they played with a sense of calm and poise, leading to smart decisions and crisp passes that always found their man. At this point, the Knicks have seen it all together, and they aren't fazed by the pressure.

What makes the Knicks so hard to beat is that they only get better in the clutch, and it's not just Brunson who beats you. Tonight, practically everyone had their moment, highlighting the depth and versatility of the defending champions.

As Kawhi Leonard deals with swelling in his left knee, his status remains a mystery , leaving the Raptors without their best player. They clearly missed him tonight, but how much will his return actually change for this team? Other than Scottie Barnes and RJ Barrett, the Raptors don't have nearly enough depth or talent to keep up with the likes of the 76ers, Celtics, or Pistons in the East. They traded away their best perimeter scorer ( Brandon Ingram ) and gave up a promising young athlete in Gradey Dick.

What the Raptors really lack is a center. Jakob Poeltl came off the bench tonight in favor of Collin Murray-Boyles , who finished with just eight points, one rebound, three assists, one steal, and three blocks on 66.7% shooting from the field. Sensing their advantage in the frontcourt, the Knicks were feasting inside, going in for easy layups and controlling the glass for a 44-23 rebounding advantage.

While there's no doubt the Raptors will be better off for Kawhi's return, they cannot rely on him to come back and just resolve their issues. To salvage this season, more proactive measures are required, and the options are limitless.

The Knicks' bench was a cause for concern going into the season, and it didn't build confidence when their best bench scorer from last season ( Jordan Clarkson ) started seeing reduced minutes. Fortunately, veteran Landry Shamet has been filling the role just fine, and he gave the Knicks another fine showing tonight. In 24 minutes off the bench, he put up 12 points, one rebound, and one assist on 57.1% shooting from the field (2-4 from three).

As the Raptors struggled to get anything from their second unit, Landry Shamet carried the Knicks' bench to ensure his team never lost momentum. His versatility let him fit into various lineups, and he made few mistakes while providing a steady boost on the court. So while Shamet may not be the hero Knicks fans were expecting, he's becoming a big storyline for their turnaround this season, and his importance is undeniable.

Ultimately, the Knicks will always lean more on their star-studded starting lineup, but having that boost off the bench makes everything easier. Tonight, we saw the impact Shamet could have (+26) and why we can expect to see more of him over the course of the season.

articles.title: Victor Wembanyama’s ridiculous self-assisted dunk steals the show despite Spurs’ 105-93 loss to Pistons
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama produced another highlight-reel moment against the Detroit Pistons, throwing the ball off the backboard before catching it and finishing wi...
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama produced another highlight-reel moment against the Detroit Pistons, throwing the ball off the backboard before catching it and finishing with a one-handed dunk.

The San Antonio Spurs star used his incredible height and creativity to get past Ausar Thompson early in their meeting with Detroit.

Wembanyama had already been blocked by one of the Thompson twins this season, but he found a different way to attack the basket this time.

Victor Wembanyama's self-assisted dunk steals the show against Detroit Pistons

The 22-year-old drove towards the paint just over a minute into the game before sensing pressure from Thompson. Rather than force his way through the defence, Wembanyama threw the ball against the backboard, collected it in the air and threw down a one-handed finish.

It was a reminder of the unusual skills that make the Frenchman such a difficult player to defend. At 7-foot-4, Wembanyama has the size to dominate near the rim, but his ability to improvise makes him even more dangerous.

He entered the contest averaging 28.6 points and 11.6 rebounds through 14 appearances, ranking third and fifth in the NBA in those categories respectively.

However, the highlight did not tell the full story of the night for San Antonio.

Despite Wembanyama finishing with 25 points and 18 rebounds, the Spurs fell to a 105-93 defeat against Detroit at the Frost Bank Center. Dylan Harper added 20 points, while Julian Champagnie scored 14.

Detroit also had the final say in the battle of the big moments, with Cade Cunningham producing a poster dunk over Wembanyama near the end of the first quarter.

The defeat leaves San Antonio with a 12-3 record after starting the season strongly.

articles.title: Total Chess: GM Abhimanyu Mishra would prefer being world champion to world No. 1 tag
articles.summary: BUDAPEST: The chubby little boy who became the world’s youngest Grandmaster at the age of 12 in 2021 is now more mature and his baby fat gave way for a
articles.body: BUDAPEST: The chubby little boy who became the world’s youngest Grandmaster at the age of 12 in 2021 is now more mature and his baby fat gave way for a more chiselled look. American Abhimanyu Mishra admits a lot has changed, apart from appearance, since he attained the title.“Before becoming a Grandmaster, I was quite rigid,” Abhimanyu told TOI on the sidelines of Total Chess Pilot here in the Hungarian capital. “I would only play like one line. I used to either play only E4 or D4, and I would stick with that for many games at a time.”That, of course, was making it easy for his opponents to understand him. “So in the past couple years, I’ve made a conscious decision to play tons of different openings, lik against Magnus (Carlsen during their match here). I played Italian D6, which I’ve never played in my life. And just the idea of being open to new openings has helped shape my understanding in a much better way.”Given a choice between becoming a world champion or a world No. 1, Abhimanyu would always pick the former. “To become a world champion, you have to win the Candidates and then have to beat someone in a match,” he explained the thrilling equation.For the forthcoming World Championship match, Abhimanyu gives Javokhir Sindarov a slight edge over D Gukesh. However, it will be a tough battle.His Indian connection is quite strong as his father is from Bhopal and mother from Agra. However, having been born and brought up in the US, Mishra has no illusions about his nationality.Chess is his sole interest as far as sports is concerned. His parents do watch cricket, but for Abhimanyu, a passing glance at the TV is all he can concede.(The writer is in Budapest at the invitation of Total Chess)Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.standfirst: "Madrid no puede renunciar a unos Juegos Olímpicos, pero Madrid tampoco los puede perder; hay que presentarse cuando existan las garantías de que nos los van a dar"
articles.summary: "Madrid no puede renunciar a unos Juegos Olímpicos, pero Madrid tampoco los puede perder; hay que presentarse cuando existan las garantías de que nos los van a dar"
articles.body: Alejandro Blanco, presidente del Comité Olímpico Español (COE), concedió una entrevista al programa 'Radioestadio Noche' de Onda Cero en la que habló sobre la posibilidad de que Madrid organice unos Juegos Olímpicos en el futuro. "Madrid es la mejor ciudad del mundo para organizar unos Juegos Olímpicos, nos lo deben", dejó claro. El candidato a la presidencia de la Asociación de Comités Olímpicos Nacionales, "es algo que no me había planteado pero que hayan pensado en mí, que confíen en mí es una gran alegría y responsabilidad", recalcó que "Madrid no puede renunciar a unos Juegos Olímpicos, pero Madrid tampoco los puede perder; hay que presentarse cuando existan las garantías de que nos los van a dar". Alejandro Blanco fue muy contundente ante Raúl Granado a la hora de pedir que la final del Mundial 2030 de fútbol se celebre en España: "Un Mundial 2030 sin final en España es un Mundial incompleto, inimaginable para mí; Infantino sabe lo que tiene que hacer". "Hay que sentarse con Infantino y explicarle las cosas: somos el país campeón del mundo masculino, femenino y en todas las categorías...y no me vas a dar el partido inaugural y la final....? Es imposible", apuntó. Alejandro Blanco destacó que "el pádel viene muy fuerte, para ser olímpico pronto, además sería muy bueno para nosotros". "Saúl Craviotto es un fuera de serie y si se está preparando para ir a Los Ángeles es que va a ir y va a competir", compartió. Alejandro Blanco también habló sobre Rafa Nadal y su futuro como directivo del Real Madrid. "Rafael Nadal puede ser lo que quiera; ha sido el deportista más admirado en el mundo por el resto de deportistas. Le veo consiguiendo lo que él quiera, si quiere ser presidente del Madrid, pues presidente del Madrid", declaró.

articles.title: World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen didn't show up for fast classical chess: Who is at fault?
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: During the players' group photoshoot before the Total Chess Pilot event in Budapest, Hungary, five-time world champion and current World No.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: During the players' group photoshoot before the Total Chess Pilot event in Budapest, Hungary, five-time world champion and current World No. 1 Magnus Carlsen was one of the last to arrive, climbing a couple of stairs to sneak into the group photo from the back and finding his place beside Kazakh Grandmaster Bibisara Assaubayeva.Soon, cutouts and clips of the two standing together started doing the rounds, captioned along the lines of "no weak characters" and "imagine the number of World Championships they share between them" — 23 in total, Carlsen alone accounting for 20.Little did anyone know that both would end up sitting across the board in a match to decide 17th-21st place in this pilot event, and that one of them choosing not to show up for the day's final game would put them at the centre of a heated debate.What happened?Carlsen had already sealed the match before a single Fast Classical move was played. He beat Assaubayeva 3-0 in Blitz with one draw, and 2-0 in Rapid, putting the score at 11.5-0.5. The match was decided, regardless of what happened next.Before the Fast Classical round began, Carlsen walked out of the playing hall. Asked why by Norwegian media outlet TV2, he said, "There will be no classical game as I understood, the match is over. The only consequence of not showing up is that you will lose a totally useless game. I think that if you play a World Championship and it counts for points and such, I can understand. But this is not a show tournament. If the match is done, it's done. In the end, if you play games after, it shall not be rated because it's always been like that. And if they want to do things differently here... yeah. This is my decision on this topic."After the mandatory 15-minute default period, Assaubayeva walked out too, awarded the win on forfeit. Day 1 of the semifinal closed 11.5-8.5 in Carlsen's favour. The game, which was supposed to count towards FIDE ratings, went unplayed and therefore had no impact on either player's classical rating.What the rules sayChief arbiter Anastasia Sorokina, speaking to ChessBase India at the venue, confirmed that any further penalties for the forfeit would be at the organisers' discretion."The result is minus-plus because Magnus didn't appear for the game. From our perspective as arbiters, there are no extra penalties for this, except the game is minus-plus, of course," she said."There is a point about the possible fees that organisers could apply, but it's not directly connected to the game. So it depends on the situation, organisers will decide."Under FIDE's regulations, forfeited games don't count toward classical ratings, which is precisely what made the decision rational for Carlsen.He'd had a torn group stage in the Fast Classical format, failing to win any of his 10 games, drawing nine and losing one to Armenia's Haik Martirosyan, a run that cost him 21.8 Elo points and pushed his live rating down to 2801.2, uncomfortably close to Hikaru Nakamura and Fabiano Caruana overtaking him as World No. 1.A draw against Assaubayeva would have cost him 3.5 more rating points, a defeat 8.5. By forfeiting, he avoided both, since an unplayed game carries no rating consequence at all.What the organisers sayTotal Chess founder and CEO Kjell Madland also shared his view on the situation."He (Carlsen) was there and discussed it with the arbiter team. The system is to win the day, and he had already won enough points to win the day. So then he didn't want to play the last game, and he didn't need to do it," he told ChessBase India.On whether Assaubayeva was informed beforehand, he replied, "No, because he could play if he wanted to play. We of course didn't discuss this with Bibisara before, that was not necessary."Pressed on whether the rules might change after this forfeit, Madland added, "The rules are the same for everyone. We can't do any differences between the players. It's the same for everyone. So if that happens tomorrow with someone else, it happened."Calling Budapest "an important learning exercise" ahead of the tour's inaugural edition in March 2027, the organisers stressed they weren't approaching the feedback "with a predetermined view that the rules need to change".The argument of moralityWhatever the rules allowed, there was a simpler courtesy Carlsen could have extended and chose not to. By his own account, and the organisers’, he had already decided against playing and discussed the matter with the arbiter team before the round began. The decision, therefore, had been made well before Assaubayeva took her seat at the board.However, with no prior communication, Assaubayeva was left waiting through the full 15-minute default period for an opponent who had no intention of showing up.The rulebook may have little to say about such omissions, governing forfeits rather than the courtesy of forewarning, but it is difficult to separate the question of sportsmanship from the technicalities of the regulations.A simple two-line message through the arbiters would have cost Carlsen nothing and spared Assaubayeva an entirely unnecessary wait.That it never came makes this less a question of what the rules required and more one of the basic consideration an opponent deserves.What the players sayAmerican Grandmaster Hans Niemann took to social media to voice his concerns. "It was already known that we have to play all the games, we talked about it in the technical meeting," he wrote on X."It's incredibly disappointing to see continued favouritism towards one player. Let's not forget the jeans, and 'Co World Champion' saga. All rules must be applied equally, regardless of the player."Alireza Firouzja noted the same technical meeting had addressed it directly, though Norwegian outlet TV2 reported Carlsen wasn't present for that meeting.Wesley So, on the other hand, saw little wrong with the logic."I think Magnus' decision was understandable. He already won the match, and if he lost to Bibi, he loses 9 points and the No. 1 spot. I don't see yet why Magnus was wrong," he wrote on X.What it leaves the organisers withEvery answer in this saga is technically correct, and that's precisely the problem. The rules allowed it, the arbiters applied them without penalty, and Carlsen broke no regulation in walking out.But a pilot event exists to surface exactly this kind of gap, between what the rulebook permits and what the field considers fair, before it hardens into precedent.India's Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa, who lost 19.3 rating points of his own in this pilot event, raised a broader gripe about dead-rubber games."It doesn't matter if you finish sixth in the group stage, you still have to play, which is kind of, honestly, sad," he said in an interview with Total Chess. "By that point the player has already started thinking about the next tournament, but he still has to play a game."With the inaugural Total Chess World Championship Tour arriving in March 2027, the organisation now has a concrete decision to make: whether a dead-rubber game, once a match is mathematically settled, should exist at all, or whether, if it does, every player is held to showing up regardless of stakes.Leaving that ambiguous is what turned one player's rational choice into a credibility question for the format itself.It also calls for a separate conversation about the structure of a tournament like this, with some players seemingly unhappy with the number of games scheduled each day across the different formats."I just felt envious that you can solve the sports part in Rapid and Blitz portion and then have a nice evening without chess, which is understandable because we have five days in a row with two rounds every day," Russian Grandmaster Ian Nepomniachtchi told ChessBase India. "Of course, there was a rest day, but it was overall a bit tiring."Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: India level lawn bowls series vs New Zealand
articles.summary: India produced a stirring comeback to defeat New Zealand 3-2 in the second lawn bowls test in Auckland on Tuesday, drawing level in the three-match series
articles.body: India produced a stirring comeback to defeat New Zealand 3-2 in the second lawn bowls test in Auckland on Tuesday, drawing level in the three-match series after losing the opening contest a day earlier.India began the second test on a positive note as the experienced Jharkhand combination of Dinesh Kumar and Sunil Bahadur registered a 6-4 victory in the men’s pairs. New Zealand responded strongly in the women’s pairs, handing Reshma Kumari and Pinki Singh a 0-9 defeat to level the contest.The momentum swung back in India’s favour in the mixed fours, where the Indian quartet combined to secure a 5-2 victory and restore the visitors’ advantage. India then wrapped up the test win with an emphatic 8-4 triumph in the first mixed pairs event. Although New Zealand claimed the second mixed pairs contest 8-2, the visitors had already done enough to secure a 3-2 victory in the test.Bowling Federation of India president Ravi Bengani credited the team’s response to its determination to bounce back from the opening-day defeat.“The team came into the second test on Tuesday with renewed vigour and ample hunger to prove to everybody that they are a powerful force to reckon with and aren’t going to take defeats lying down,” he said from Auckland.According to Bengani, the fightback had actually begun in the latter stages of Monday’s opening test after India recovered from losing the first three events to win both mixed pairs contests. “It was an amazing comeback, especially after we had lost the first three events on Monday in the first test. Our rebound started on Monday itself, particularly after we lost the first three matches,” he said.The BFI president also praised Reshma after the youngster endured a difficult outing in the women’s pairs. “She bounced back really well in the later games on Tuesday after the initial setback in the women’s pairs, where she couldn’t produce a performance that reflected her true potential and capabilities,” Bengani said.India’s victory levels the series at 1-1 and sets up a winner-takes-all third and final test, with the visitors carrying momentum into the decider after one of their most resilient performances of the tour.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
